aliases: Omega Sense Inventory and Identity Matrix

sources.note: Chronological forensic reconstruction of every sense of the symbol Omega across corpus steps 231-267 (plus a follow-up sweep of the whole corpus): five in-window senses, a ten-pair identity matrix, and self-corrections finding the corpus had already registered the sharpest homonym as TG-15/C-06 and a governance ruling GN-09/D-R27 already exists (though it does not cover Omega-1/2/3).

rows.anchor: A search defect found first, and it changes the count ... A glyph-only search returns 1 file of 11 and 2 occurrences of 28 — a 93% miss.
rows.statement: Finds the corpus writes the symbol Omega two ways (Unicode glyph Omega and LaTeX \Omega): across steps 231-267 there are 28 total occurrences in 11 of 40 files, but a glyph-only search finds only 2 occurrences in 1 file -- a 93% miss rate -- establishing that any symbol sweep for this corpus must cover both notations.

rows.anchor: Ω Sense Inventory — FIVE senses ... (Ω-1 ontology, Ω-2 observation, Ω-3 transition arg, Ω-4 state measure space, Ω-5 generic placeholder)
rows.statement: Reconstructs five distinct in-window Omega senses with birth documents and identity status: Omega-1 'ontology' (Omega=domain ontology/rules, born 025k L53 2026-08-28 09:39, status CONTINUOUS within its family then RE-FOUNDED AWAY at 031); Omega-2 'observation' (Omega:W->O, defined 031 SS31.18 2026-08-28 10:22 as the observation mechanism, status IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED though byte-identical in type to 031); Omega-3 'transition arg' (untyped 4th argument of delta_K(K_t,o_t,rho_t,Omega_t), born step-016 L1993 2026-08-27 16:00, the OLDEST readable Omega, IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED, its own sources say the signature is unresolved); Omega-4 'state measure space' (Omega=K, the sample space IS the knowledge-state space, born 238 L16 during the R1 measure-theory phase, EXPLICITLY_REDEFINED then abandoned as a 'temptation'); Omega-5 'generic placeholder' (borrowed textbook notation for algebra/measurement/probability-space conventions, never a KnowledgeOS object, classified HOMONYM).

rows.anchor: ⛔ Correction to my own prior finding ... Net: 6 → 5 senses, with one previously invisible collision inside a single document.
rows.statement: Corrects the investigation's own prior claim (09-EVIDENCE-LOG.md SS5) that Omega has six mutually incompatible meanings: that count over-counted Omega-4 across three retrospective-citation sites as three separate senses, under-attributed Omega:W->O's definitional source (031 SS31.18, two days before the 251 citation), and missed both Omega-1 (the 025-series ontology sense, co-occurring 300 lines from Omega:W->O in the same document step_251) and Omega-5 (236's explicit 'a set of operations' gloss). Net correction: 6 senses collapses to 5, revealing a previously invisible collision (Omega-1 and Omega-2 coexisting unremarked within a single document, step_251).

rows.anchor: Ω_a / Ω_b / Ω_c — an explicit split record whose terms are never defined [later WITHDRAWN, see §12.1] ... The role survived as an invariant; whether the SYMBOL continued to denote it is a separate question the corpus does not answer.
rows.statement: Records step_238's assertion that Omega diverged into three roles (Omega_a->IdealState/contract, Omega_b->dropped, Omega_c->complement principle => invariant I-7: X_t != Observed(X_t)) with no document (in the initially searched forms) defining the three terms individually; notes the ROLE carried by Omega_c demonstrably survives as invariant I-7 with the same semantics as Omega:W->O, but the corpus never states that the SYMBOL Omega_c became Omega:W->O -- recorded as IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED, not continuity. (This claim about Omega_a/b/c being undefined is itself later withdrawn in section 12.1 of the same file upon a wider evidence sweep.)

rows.anchor: 4. Ω : W → O — located, typed, and its inheritance tested ... retained / weakened / altered / abandoned? RETAINED, unchanged, at the one site that carries it.
rows.statement: Traces Omega:W->O to its definitional source (031 SS31.18 L598, boxed, 2026-08-28 10:22:51, with W_t='the relevant real-world state' and O_t=Obs(W_t) the partial observation) and tests inheritance: only step_251 (18:36, two days later) carries the byte-identical W->O signature, and it does so via an unattributed citation to 'the corpus' with no step number or explicit equivalence claim -- every other in-window Omega has a different or absent type. Status: RETAINED unchanged at the one site that carries it.

rows.anchor: 5. Four histories, kept separate (Conceptual / Mathematical / Operational / Governance) ... A later mathematical redefinition has not overwritten an earlier conceptual record here — because there was never a redefinition. There were independent definitions that never met.
rows.statement: Separates four independent histories for Omega: Conceptual (four unrelated referents -- derivation rule-set, world-to-observation mechanism, an unnamed fourth transition argument, and the space of possible knowledge states -- with no conceptual thread connecting them); Mathematical (one function W->O, one rule set, one measure-space carrier, one untyped argument, one borrowed placeholder -- only Omega-2 has a definitionally stated signature); Operational (Omega-1 consumed by Update/Derive, Omega-3 by delta_K, Omega-2 never consumed by any operation in the window, Omega-4 demoted from foundation to regime to 'temptation', Omega-5 never operational); Governance/history (R1, Omega-4's home, is classified a 'failed direction' with ALT-01 recorded -- but this claim of 'no governance act on Omega itself' is later withdrawn in section 12.2). Concludes there was never a redefinition overwriting an earlier record -- these were independent definitions that never met.

rows.anchor: 6. Re-foundings — one explicit alignment, and it is the whole finding ... The symbol Ω crossed re-founding #1 and was re-used for a different object. Silently.
rows.statement: Checks Omega's alignment against five known corpus re-foundings, finding only one decisive alignment: re-founding #1 (031, 'drops the 025 apparatus') explicitly drops the Omega-1=domain-ontology apparatus and, in the same document 43 minutes later, defines Omega:W->O as the observation mechanism, mentioning '025', 'domain ontology' or Update(K,E,Omega,EC) zero times. Re-foundings #2/#3/#5 show no Omega evidence; re-founding #4 (262, K=(A,R)) shows no alignment since Omega had already gone dark 51 minutes earlier; a shared classification with tau:SxC->S (Step 204) as sibling 'family' rows is explicitly recorded as classification only, not shared identity. Concludes the symbol Omega crossed re-founding #1 and was silently re-used for a different object.

rows.anchor: 7. G-19 not used ... no Ω sense was preferred because it makes the K model work.
rows.statement: Explicitly records that no primary source connects the G-19 falsification result to any Omega sense, and no Omega sense was adjudicated or preferred on the grounds that it makes the K model work -- an independence discipline note.

rows.anchor: 8. Identity matrix — all ten pairs ... Not one pair of the ten is supported as the same object by any corpus evidence.
rows.statement: Builds a complete ten-pair identity matrix over the five senses: Omega-1xOmega-2 HOMONYM (explicit, 43 minutes apart, type-incompatible, coexisting unremarked 300 lines apart in step_251); Omega-2xOmega-3 DISTINCT by explicit differentiation (step-016 separately names Obs(X_t,S_t) and a different fourth argument Omega_t in the same boxed formula); Omega-1xOmega-4, Omega-1xOmega-5, Omega-2xOmega-4, Omega-2xOmega-5 DISTINCT by type; Omega-1xOmega-3, Omega-3xOmega-4, Omega-3xOmega-5 UNDECIDABLE (Omega-3 untyped, sources say so); Omega-4xOmega-5 POSSIBLE SAME OBJECT-identity-unwitnessed (both measure-theoretic sample-space notation, but Omega-4 commits to Omega=K while Omega-5 is a placeholder). Tally: 1 HOMONYM, 1 DISTINCT-by-differentiation, 4 DISTINCT-by-type, 3 UNDECIDABLE, 1 POSSIBLE-SAME-UNWITNESSED, 0 SAME OBJECT -- not one of the ten pairs is supported as the same object by any corpus evidence.

rows.anchor: 9. Mandatory adversarial check — both directions ... The corpus had the instrument and did not turn it on itself.
rows.statement: Runs a two-directional adversarial evidence check: (A) searching for evidence that senses ARE one continuous object -- no identifying statement, rename/supersession/retirement record, or type bridge found, so results are recorded IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED rather than assumed distinct; (B) searching for evidence senses ARE distinct -- finds two incompatible explicit definitions (025k vs 031, 43 minutes apart, neither citing the other), one document (step-016) naming the observation function Obs while using Omega for a different argument, and step_238's own explicit 'Same word != Same concept' DDD-lesson collision-marking rule (applied there to Zero and Lord). The self-referential finding: step_238 states this exact discipline as a lesson, applies it to Zero and Lord, and in the same document uses Omega in three different senses without applying the lesson to Omega itself -- the corpus had the instrument and did not turn it on itself.

rows.anchor: 10. Findings G22-1 through G22-8
rows.statement: Issues eight findings: G22-1 (CRITICAL) Omega-1xOmega-2 is a HOMONYM on explicit definitional evidence, born 43 minutes apart across re-founding #1, neither citing the other; G22-2 (CRITICAL) step_251 carries both senses simultaneously 300 lines apart and never notices, the same document G-03's Omega/EC sub-family classification rests on; G22-3 (HIGH, corrective) five senses not six, correcting an over-split of Omega-4 and a missed Omega-1/Omega-5; G22-4 (CRITICAL, method) a glyph-only search misses 93% of Omega occurrences in this window; G22-5 (HIGH) Omega-3 is the oldest readable Omega (step-016, 2026-08-27) and untyped at birth with a second undefined argument rho_t alongside it; G22-6 (UNRESOLVED, HIGH) the Omega_a/b/c split is asserted with three named roles and zero types; G22-7 (UNRESOLVED, MEDIUM) no governance act touches Omega -- rename/supersession/retirement/collision record absent; G22-8 (MEDIUM) step_238 states 'Same word != Same concept' as a DDD lesson, applies it to Zero and Lord, yet itself uses Omega in three senses in the same document.

rows.anchor: 11. Scope discipline ... Ω-4's own sources call it a 'failed direction' and a 'temptation' — that is their classification, recorded, not adopted. ... Firewall: brainstorming/three_model_convergence/ was not opened
rows.statement: Scopes the investigation: no sense is preferred, merged, repaired or retired; Omega-4's own sources' self-classification as a 'failed direction'/'temptation' is recorded, not adopted as the investigation's own judgment; three documents outside the 231-267 window were opened solely to type a symbol used inside it, importing no other content. Discloses the standing firewall: brainstorming/three_model_convergence/ was not opened, read, grepped or cited.

rows.anchor: 12.1 ⛔ Ω_a / Ω_b / Ω_c ARE defined — two days before 238 cites them ... 238 reports as settled what its source recorded as unresolved, with no derivation shown.
rows.statement: Retracts the earlier §3 claim: a wider evidence sweep (3,108 files, 493 containing Omega) finds Omega_a/Omega_b/Omega_c ARE defined, two days before step_238 cites them, in combine-prompt-4 (2026-08-28 15:01:40): Omega-a=ideal reference->Ideal State->Epistemic Contract, Omega-b=unboundedness->dropped, Omega-c=whole-space observation->unresolved. The miss was a notation-form defect (searched subscript \Omega_a rather than the corpus's dominant hyphenated Omega-a form), yielding the methodological correction that symbol sweeps must cover both subscript and hyphen forms. Also finds step_238 changed Omega-c's fate from 'unresolved' (source) to 'complement principle -> invariant I-7' with no derivation shown, and that two downstream records disagree on where Omega-c went (DISPLACED-no-host per combine-prompt-4/lord-omega-analysis vs TRANSFORMED-into-its-complement per 238/phase-2d-closure), recorded as unreconciled.

rows.anchor: 12.2 ⛔ A governance ruling on Ω does exist ... Ω is ruled historical-only and excluded from the final ubiquitous language, on a reconstructed lineage basis ... Three of the five in-window senses are outside the scope of the only ruling that exists.
rows.statement: Retracts the earlier §5 claim that no governance act touches Omega: finds GN-09 (governance-notes.md L67, an 'Omega terminology ruling' -- Omega belongs to theory/history, not the final ubiquitous language, retained in the discovery record to explain the architecture's evolution), D-R27 (A3-definition-register.md L56, ruling Omega 'historical term only' and decomposing Omega-a->EC, Omega-b bounded away, Omega-c->X_t per GN-09, marked RECONSTRUCTED lineage ruling), and OQ-6 (Omega-b's drop recorded as an open record gap, 'dropped by disuse, no act'). Notes the corrected governance line rules Omega historical-only and excluded from the final ubiquitous language on a reconstructed-lineage basis, but this ruling governs only the Omega-a/b/c decomposition -- it does not mention Omega-1 (domain ontology), Omega-2 (Omega:W->O) or Omega-3 (delta_K's argument), leaving three of the five in-window senses outside the only ruling that exists.

rows.anchor: 12.3 ⛔ The corpus had already registered the collision — and I re-derived it ... This is the G-19 pattern again, and this time I am inside it.
rows.statement: Finds the corpus's verification lane had already registered the Omega overload eleven days earlier: TG-15 (THEORY-GAP-REGISTER.md L39, 2026-08-30 20:51) states 'Omega carries >=4 global senses, two of them foundational and opposite in direction... OPEN -- NEW, and the most dangerous naming collision found'; C-06 (11-CONTRADICTION-REGISTRY.md L17, 2026-08-30 21:16) states 'Omega = Knowledge Space vs Omega:W->O... TRUE CONTRADICTION... Unregistered by every prior pass.' Explicitly names this as a repeat of the G-19 pattern (a claimed absence was actually already executed/registered elsewhere) -- this time the investigation itself is inside that pattern. Notes what survives as genuinely new: TG-15's four senses (sample space, Knowledge Space, observation function, residual possibilities) do not include Omega-1 (domain ontology/rules, 025k L53), so the Omega-1 x Omega-2 homonym, its 43-minute interval, and its coincidence with re-founding #1 remain unrecorded elsewhere in the corpus.

rows.anchor: 12.4 A sixth sense, out of window — and it is the other half of C-06 ... Ω-7 Knowledge Space ... Zero(K_t) = Ω \ Represented(K_t)
rows.statement: Adds a sixth/out-of-window sense Omega-7 'Knowledge Space' (from a 2026-08-26 Zero-lens research-synthesis document and three further files: Zero(K_t)=Omega\Represented(K_t), Omega as the infinite knowledge space of which any K_t is a partial projection). Notes Omega-7 is C-06's first (Knowledge-Space) term, does not occur in the 231-267 window, but is the sense the corpus itself judged most dangerous, and is the direct ancestor of Omega-a ('ideal reference'), making it upstream of the whole Omega_a/b/c decomposition.

rows.anchor: 12.5 An attribution in an independent verification that does not reproduce ... Two of the four Ω-origin attributions in that sentence do not reproduce. ... A wrong citation is not weak evidence for the identity — it is no evidence
rows.statement: Checks a downstream verification claim (TV-F-022-024) attributing four Omega-overload origin sites (step-007, step-008, step-016 SS54, step-017) and finds two do not reproduce at source: the cited formula F(K0,H,rho,Omega) does not occur anywhere in the universe (step-016 SS54 actually contains two separate boxed formulas, K(t)=Fold(...) and delta_K(K_t,o_t,rho_t,Omega_t), which the citation conflates); the claimed gloss 'Omega=ontology' in step-016 is unsupported (step-016 has exactly one Omega with no gloss); and step-017 contains ZERO Omega occurrences of either spelling. Concludes a wrong citation is not weak evidence for an identity claim but no evidence at all, and that adopting it would have wrongly made Omega-1 x Omega-3 read as SAME OBJECT on nothing at all -- so Omega-1 x Omega-3 stays UNDECIDABLE.

rows.anchor: 12.6 Ω after the window — G-11 is far larger than recorded ... Ω_K = the set of legitimate kernel operations ... Kṛṣṇa ≡ Ω: explicitly REJECTED
rows.statement: Finds Omega's post-window (steps 268-292) footprint is far larger than previously recorded: 171 files, 64 containing Omega, 290 line-occurrences, becoming central to the Gita lane (step_286) with at least three further readings -- Omega=Sanjaya=observation capability (Omega-2 revived, connecting to the B0050 sanjaya-observation-layer object, corpus-native per the reviewer), Omega=epistemic horizon/infinite Knowledge Space with K_t proper-subset-of Omega (Omega-7 revived), and Omega_K=the set of legitimate kernel operations (Omega-5's operation-set reading, now promoted to a genuine KnowledgeOS object) -- while Krsna=Omega is explicitly REJECTED as a 'rejected metaphysical projection'. Concludes the two senses C-06 calls a TRUE CONTRADICTION are both live again after step 285, unreconciled, and G-11 must be re-scoped from 'Omega and EC reappear at step 282' to 'Omega re-enters across 64 files in at least three senses, two ruled contradictory'.

rows.anchor: 12.7 Convergent corroboration of the 2026-08-24 origin ... Two independent passes, same two files of 92 dated that day, same characterisation. The G-21 gate verdict is unchanged and now double-sourced.
rows.statement: Reports that this investigation's independent identification of Omega's origin files (2026-08-24) matches the corpus's own archaeology (AF-003, phase-archaeology-findings.md, 2026-08-28 17:35: 'Omega first appears 2026-08-24 in kernel lens docs as the ambient space of typed/Bayesian models -- one day before phase_measure_theory opens; the measure-theory crisis inherited Omega, it did not coin it') exactly -- two independent passes agreeing on the same two files (of 92 dated that day) and the same characterization, leaving the pre-existing G-21 gate verdict unchanged but now double-sourced.

rows.anchor: 12.8 Net effect on the disposition (before/after table)
rows.statement: Summarizes the net effect of the section-12 evidence sweep in a before/after table: in-window senses unchanged at 5; out-of-window senses grow from 1 to 2 (adding Omega-7); Omega_a/b/c goes from 'never defined' to defined 08-28 15:01 with 238 having altered Omega-c's recorded fate; governance goes from 'no act' to GN-09+D-R27 found (though not covering Omega-1/2/3); prior art on the collision goes from 'none found' to TG-15 and C-06 found; the Omega-1xOmega-2 HOMONYM finding remains STILL NEW since Omega-1 appears in none of TG-15's four senses; Omega-1xOmega-3 remains UNDECIDABLE, now with a refuted attribution attached; the G-21 gate remains open with its constraint unchanged, now double-sourced.

rows.anchor: G-11 ... G-22 §12.6: 64 of 171 files, 290 occurrences ... Both terms of C-06 live again ... massively under-scoped as 'reappear at step 282 (Ω=2, EC=5)'
rows.statement: G-11 (do Omega/EC re-entering at step 282 mean re-entry or a third meaning?): imports G-22 SS12.6's finding of 64 of 171 files / 290 occurrences across steps 269-291 in at least 3 senses (Omega=Sanjaya revived, Omega=epistemic horizon/K_t proper-subset-Omega revived, Omega_K=legitimate kernel operations; Krsna=Omega rejected), with both terms of the C-06 true-contradiction live again. Verdict: the gap as originally stated ('reappear at step 282, Omega=2, EC=5') was massively under-scoped. Action: RE-SCOPE (already applied in the G-22 commit).

rows.anchor: G-21 ... G-22 §12.7 + AF-003: same two files of 92 ... the measure-theory crisis inherited Ω; it did not coin it ... referent identified — for Ω-4/Ω-5 only; Ω-1/Ω-2/Ω-3 origins remain unlocated ... RE-SCOPE, KEEP OPEN — per sense
rows.statement: G-21 (is Omega's 'kernel era, 2026-08-24' provenance claim real?): confirms via G-22 SS12.7 and the independent AF-003 archaeology finding (same two files of 92 dated that day; 'the measure-theory crisis inherited Omega; it did not coin it') that the 2026-08-24 provenance is real for the Omega-4/Omega-5 senses specifically, but the origins of Omega-1, Omega-2 and Omega-3 remain unlocated. Action: RE-SCOPE per-sense and KEEP OPEN for the still-unlocated senses.

rows.anchor: And Satisfied is a three-way homonym in one document ... three types under one name. The same defect as Ω-1 × Ω-2, inside one document, on one object, and already recorded in the verification lane.
rows.statement: Finds 'Satisfied' is used as three different types within one document (025d): an element of the status set S, a set-valued function Satisfied(K,R_G), and a predicate Satisfied(K,r,EC) -- explicitly identified as the same homonym defect pattern as the Omega-1 x Omega-2 collision, occurring inside one document on one object, and already recorded in the verification lane. Re-poses G-01 as three distinct questions: (i) why Zero carries six irreconcilable forms in 025d; (ii) why G is dropped at 25D.24 and replaced by K* at 25D.31; (iii) what fixes S after 11 values. The prior Gamma(E,Q,C,EC)-relocation framing is withdrawn as superseded, since EC was never lost.

rows.anchor: 5. ⭐⭐ A challenge to G-19's and G-22's independence language ... Every execution G-19 found (20:47, 21:05, 21:13) is after Step 258. ... Amended wording adopted: 'executed without reference to the commission' — replaces 'independently'
rows.statement: Challenges the word 'independent' as used in the G-19 and G-22 findings by citing the master register's own G-13 (EXECUTED, CRITICAL): 'primary and secondary corpora are interleaved and mutually citing after ~Step 258, within minutes... agreement between them is not independent corroboration', recommending 'freeze one tree'. Notes every execution G-19 found (20:47, 21:05, 21:13) falls after Step 258, so while the per-document fact that none cites Step 268 and none is cited by the commissioning lane still stands as checked, the general inference of independence is not available for this interval; G-22's AF-003 convergence (2026-08-28, before the ~258 interleaving) is judged less affected but still qualified, recorded not resolved. Adopts amended wording: 'executed without reference to the commission' replaces 'independently' throughout, as a checkable per-document fact rather than an unavailable independence claim.

rows.anchor: §1 · Population ... 44 of the 55 are step_286 — one step number ... ONE evidential lineage, not 44 confirmations. ... The two 'intervals' are not sequential — they overlap by ~44 hours ... Step numbers imply sequence; the chronology shows parallel lanes.
rows.statement: Censuses Omega in steps 269-291: 168 files, 55 containing Omega, 293 total occurrences, of which 44 cluster in a single step (s286) written within one continuous 08-31/09-01 Gita-thread session -- explicitly weighted as ONE independent evidential lineage rather than 44 separate confirmations. Discovers the '269-291' and '231-267' windows are NOT sequential: the last Omega occurrence in the 231-267 window (s266, 2026-08-30 19:54:50) comes AFTER the first Omega occurrence in the 269-291 window (s286, 2026-08-28 23:52:31) -- the later-numbered window begins 1 day 20 hours before the earlier-numbered window ends, proving step numbers do not imply chronological sequence and the two ranges represent parallel, not sequential, lanes.

rows.anchor: §2, §6 · The Ω objects in this interval, with their definitional sources (Ω-A Sañjaya/observation, Ω-B epistemic horizon, Ω-C Ω_K kernel operations, Ω-D integration/element domain) ... Ω-D contains a type error inside one file
rows.statement: Defines four live post-267 Omega senses with verbatim sources: Omega-A 'Sanjaya/observation' (08-31, boxed Omega:W->O, described as 'recovered', citing D285-6); Omega-B 'epistemic horizon' (09-01, boxed Omega=epistemic horizon, explicitly rejecting both Omega=God and Omega=K as 'unjustified architectural identities'); Omega-C 'Omega_K kernel operations' (09-01, boxed K=(K_t,Omega_K) later K=(K_t,Omega_K,I), Omega_K='legitimate/permitted kernel operations'); Omega-D 'integration/element domain' (08-28, appearing as both a measure space and a set of knowledge states). Finds an internal type error within Omega-D's own single source document: one line integrates K_t OVER Omega (making K_t a function on Omega) while another quantifies 'for all K in Omega' (making K an element of Omega) -- K cannot be both; recorded, not repaired.

rows.anchor: §5 · Three-level identity test ... does the horizon document mention Sañjaya? 0 times. does the Sañjaya document mention horizon? 0 times. ... Only ONE pair reaches Level 3: Ω-A × Ω-2. And it reaches it on a byte-identical signature with identical glosses — while citing the wrong source.
rows.statement: Runs a three-level (lexical/mathematical/semantic) identity test across all Omega-sense pairs: finds Omega-A and Omega-2 (from 031) reach full Level-3 SAME-OBJECT status with a byte-identical W->O signature and identical W/O glosses, but Omega-A mis-attributes its provenance to D285-6 rather than 031; Omega-B and Omega-4/7 are DISTINCT-EXPLICIT since the corpus explicitly rejects Omega=K; Omega-B and Omega-A are IDENTITY UNWITNESSED (neither document mentions the other, despite both being definitionally developed); Omega-C and Omega-5 (the s236 operation-set reading) are RELATED with no citation; Omega-C and O_core (s277) are RELATED-IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED; Omega-D's internal type error makes it UNDECIDABLE. Notes the two most-developed Omega senses in this interval (the horizon document and the Sanjaya document) never mention each other at all.

rows.anchor: §7 · C-06 — a local ruling against COMBINING, not a global verdict on Ω ... C-06 adjudicates that two HOMONYMS must not be combined. It does NOT rule that Ω is contradictory. ... the corpus independently reaches the same separation five days later ... CORROBORATIVE, and by §9 this counts as two lineages, not two documents.
rows.statement: Re-examines the corpus's own C-06 'TRUE CONTRADICTION' ruling (Omega=Knowledge Space vs Omega:W->O) verbatim, identifying it addresses specifically Omega-7 vs Omega-2, contradicting the 031 non-identifiability result, is a mathematical+semantic (set vs function) type incompatibility, concerns objects G-22 already classed DISTINCT, and crucially is BOUNDED/conditional ('combining them WOULD make...') rather than a global verdict. Concludes C-06 rules only that two homonyms must not be COMBINED, not that Omega itself is contradictory. Notes the corpus independently reaches the identical separation five days later via Omega-B's explicit rejection of Omega=K, in a different lane, with no citation between the two -- classified as two independent (CORROBORATIVE) lineages rather than a single duplicated finding.

rows.anchor: §12 · Continuity with apparatus loss — the Ω instance, and it is sharper than 026's ... A gap was opened for an object the corpus had DEFINED THREE DAYS EARLIER — and then closed by 'recovering' it. ... apparatus never left the corpus — only the working set — and its re-discovery was recorded as a gap closure.
rows.statement: Traces a precise sequence: 031 defines Omega:W->O boxed (08-28 10:22) -> a 155-file silence -> Omega returns (08-29) -> step_251 cites it unattributed (08-30) -> a NEW GAP is explicitly opened ('Gap 1: (W,Omega) referent layer', 08-31 19:03) -> the same gap is closed hours later by 'recovering' the Sanjaya layer (08-31 19:52, G3->G5) -> a claim that 'the earlier claim that the verification lane lacked an entire observation/referent layer is no longer valid' (08-31 19:40) -> Omega-A's document frames this as resolving 'a structural omission discovered in D285-6' (08-31 20:11). Concludes a gap was opened for an object the corpus had already defined three days earlier, then closed by 'recovering' it -- the corpus does not record this as a loss, it records it as a discovery. Contrasts this with G-12's 026 mechanism ('continuity declared, apparatus not carried'): here, the apparatus never left the corpus at all, only the ACTIVE WORKING SET did, and its re-discovery was mislabeled a gap closure -- two distinct mechanisms in one family, recorded as evidence not generalized into a law.

rows.anchor: The corpus draws the right distinction itself ... 'Observation' being recovered closes the discovery gap, but the executable semantics of Ω and Qualify are not thereby solved. Discovery gap ≠ semantic gap — stated by the corpus, and correct.
rows.statement: Notes approvingly that the corpus itself already draws the correct distinction: recovering Omega's observation-layer definition closes only a DISCOVERY gap, not the underlying SEMANTIC gap (executable semantics of Omega and Qualify remain unsolved) -- endorsed here as a stated-and-correct corpus self-observation, not a finding original to this investigation.

rows.anchor: §8 · Distributed completeness ... Ω-A COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES ... Ω-B GENUINE CORPUS GAP (bounded: Ω-B only) ... Ω-C IDENTITY UNRESOLVED ... Ω-D UNDECIDABLE
rows.statement: Tests distributed completeness per sense: Omega-A is COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES (031 supplies the non-identifiability result Omega-A itself omits); Omega-B is a GENUINE CORPUS GAP, explicitly bounded to Omega-B only -- searched across all 55 Omega files plus the whole non-firewalled corpus, no type/domain/codomain is ever given for the 'horizon' concept; Omega-C is IDENTITY UNRESOLVED (operations named but the set never enumerated; s277's O_core enumerates a candidate set with unwitnessed identity); Omega-D is UNDECIDABLE due to its internal type inconsistency.

rows.anchor: §10 · Mathematical audit (Ω-A PROVEN function W→O, Ω-B UNKNOWN never typed, Ω-C PROVEN as a set/UNKNOWN membership, Ω-D contradictory within one file) ... No TYPE-CONSTRAINED value was promoted to PROVEN. §11 · DDD audit ... Four bounded-context candidates, one glyph, zero context mappings.
rows.statement: Mathematical audit: Omega-A is PROVEN as function W->O; Omega-B is UNKNOWN, never typed at all; Omega-C is PROVEN as a finite set but its membership is UNKNOWN; Omega-D is contradictory within one file (measure space and element set simultaneously). Notes no type-constrained value in this audit was ever promoted to PROVEN status. DDD audit assigns each Omega sense to a distinct bounded context (Omega-A observation/referent layer -- map reality to observation; Omega-B epistemic framing/Gita lens -- situate a finite state against a horizon, explicitly Omega!=K and Omega!=God per the corpus; Omega-C kernel -- delimit permitted operations; Omega-D Gita-derived mathematics -- integration domain/state set), concluding four bounded-context candidates share one glyph with zero context mappings between them.

rows.anchor: §16 · Terminal conditions (8 corpus-wide Ω objects, 4 live in 269–291; classification E overall — OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, per-sense: Ω-A B, Ω-B D (genuine gap, bounded), Ω-C E, Ω-D E)
rows.statement: Answers eight terminal questions: 8 Omega objects exist corpus-wide (Omega-1..Omega-8 combining G-22 and G-12 findings), 4 live in 269-291 (A,B,C,D); genuine birth points identified (Omega-A actually born at 031, 08-28, not 08-31 as its own document implies; Omega-B 09-01 01:17; Omega-C 09-01 00:53; Omega-D 08-28 23:52); the windows overlap 44 hours; identity results are 1 SAME OBJECT (A x Omega-2), 1 DISTINCT-EXPLICIT (B x Omega-4/7), 2 RELATED (C), rest UNWITNESSED; C-06 adjudicates specifically Omega-7 x Omega-2 and is LOCAL not global; 269-291 completes 031's Omega-2 partially (restoring the signature and glosses but omitting the non-identifiability result and mis-attributing the source); exactly one genuine bounded semantic gap exists (Omega-B is never typed). Final classification: Omega as a whole = class E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, four live senses, one glyph, one Level-3 identity established, zero context mappings); per-sense Omega-A=B (complete through multiple sources), Omega-B=D (genuine gap, bounded), Omega-C=E, Omega-D=E. Explicitly notes class A was not forced onto any sense.

rows.anchor: §14 · Negative history ... Not found: any type/domain/codomain for Ω-B; any document identifying Ω-A with Ω-B; any citation from Ω-A to 031; any context mapping between the four senses. ⇒ GENUINE CORPUS GAP for Ω-B's type only; everything else IDENTITY UNWITNESSED.
rows.statement: Confirms a negative-history search across all 168 step-269-291 files (both spellings) plus the whole non-firewalled corpus for Omega-B's type finds nothing: no type/domain/codomain for Omega-B, no document identifying Omega-A with Omega-B, no citation from Omega-A back to 031, and no context mapping between the four live senses. Classifies exactly one item as GENUINE CORPUS GAP (Omega-B's type) and everything else as IDENTITY UNWITNESSED rather than gap. Confirms Det_r and any firewalled Omega history remain FIREWALL-LIMITED; firewall honoured, nothing canonicalized, no Omega sense selected or merged.

rows.anchor: §87 — δ's declared signature ... 𝕂 --E,Q,C,H/EC,ℐ--> 𝕂 ... the closest thing to a declared shape for δ found so far ... Relevant to D3 ('Γ is derived and not a component of K, so δ has nowhere to write') — here it writes 𝕂. Recorded; D3 not re-dispositioned, since this is a signature, not a commit rule. ... Ω_K — a further Ω sense (a probability sample space) ... Flagged for the Ω sense inventory; not merged here.
rows.statement: Finds SS87 gives delta the closest thing to a declared signature found so far in the corpus: K --(E,Q,C,H)/(EC,I)--> K, parameterized above by four inputs and constrained below by the contract and protected invariants. Notes relevance to a prior finding D3 ('Gamma is derived, not a component of K, so delta has nowhere to write') -- here delta explicitly writes K, though explicitly records this is only a SIGNATURE, not a commit rule, so D3 is not re-dispositioned. Also identifies SS87's probabilistic layer (Omega_K, A_K, P_K, invoked 'only when stochastic modeling is justified') as yet another distinct Omega sense (a probability sample space, distinct from the measurable carrier X used elsewhere in KS=(X,A)) -- flagged for the ongoing Omega sense inventory (G-21/G-22) but explicitly not merged here.

lexical.anchor: A search defect found first, and it changes the count ... A glyph-only search returns 1 file of 11 and 2 occurrences of 28 — a 93% miss.

formal.anchor: 8. Identity matrix — all ten pairs ... Not one pair of the ten is supported as the same object by any corpus evidence.

operational.anchor: 9. Mandatory adversarial check — both directions ... The corpus had the instrument and did not turn it on itself.

governance.anchor: 10. Findings G22-1 through G22-8

rationale_evidence.anchor: 4. Ω : W → O — located, typed, and its inheritance tested ... retained / weakened / altered / abandoned? RETAINED, unchanged, at the one site that carries it.
rationale_evidence.statement: Traces Omega:W->O to its definitional source (031 SS31.18 L598, boxed, 2026-08-28 10:22:51, with W_t='the relevant real-world state' and O_t=Obs(W_t) the partial observation) and tests inheritance: only step_251 (18:36, two days later) carries the byte-identical W->O signature, and it does so via an unattributed citation to 'the corpus' with no step number or explicit equivalence claim -- every other in-window Omega has a different or absent type. Status: RETAINED unchanged at the one site that carries it.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 5. Four histories, kept separate (Conceptual / Mathematical / Operational / Governance) ... A later mathematical redefinition has not overwritten an earlier conceptual record here — because there was never a redefinition. There were independent definitions that never met.
rationale_evidence.statement: Separates four independent histories for Omega: Conceptual (four unrelated referents -- derivation rule-set, world-to-observation mechanism, an unnamed fourth transition argument, and the space of possible knowledge states -- with no conceptual thread connecting them); Mathematical (one function W->O, one rule set, one measure-space carrier, one untyped argument, one borrowed placeholder -- only Omega-2 has a definitionally stated signature); Operational (Omega-1 consumed by Update/Derive, Omega-3 by delta_K, Omega-2 never consumed by any operation in the window, Omega-4 demoted from foundation to regime to 'temptation', Omega-5 never operational); Governance/history (R1, Omega-4's home, is classified a 'failed direction' with ALT-01 recorded -- but this claim of 'no governance act on Omega itself' is later withdrawn in section 12.2). Concludes there was never a redefinition overwriting an earlier record -- these were independent definitions that never met.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 6. Re-foundings — one explicit alignment, and it is the whole finding ... The symbol Ω crossed re-founding #1 and was re-used for a different object. Silently.
rationale_evidence.statement: Checks Omega's alignment against five known corpus re-foundings, finding only one decisive alignment: re-founding #1 (031, 'drops the 025 apparatus') explicitly drops the Omega-1=domain-ontology apparatus and, in the same document 43 minutes later, defines Omega:W->O as the observation mechanism, mentioning '025', 'domain ontology' or Update(K,E,Omega,EC) zero times. Re-foundings #2/#3/#5 show no Omega evidence; re-founding #4 (262, K=(A,R)) shows no alignment since Omega had already gone dark 51 minutes earlier; a shared classification with tau:SxC->S (Step 204) as sibling 'family' rows is explicitly recorded as classification only, not shared identity. Concludes the symbol Omega crossed re-founding #1 and was silently re-used for a different object.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 9. Mandatory adversarial check — both directions ... The corpus had the instrument and did not turn it on itself.
rationale_evidence.statement: Runs a two-directional adversarial evidence check: (A) searching for evidence that senses ARE one continuous object -- no identifying statement, rename/supersession/retirement record, or type bridge found, so results are recorded IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED rather than assumed distinct; (B) searching for evidence senses ARE distinct -- finds two incompatible explicit definitions (025k vs 031, 43 minutes apart, neither citing the other), one document (step-016) naming the observation function Obs while using Omega for a different argument, and step_238's own explicit 'Same word != Same concept' DDD-lesson collision-marking rule (applied there to Zero and Lord). The self-referential finding: step_238 states this exact discipline as a lesson, applies it to Zero and Lord, and in the same document uses Omega in three different senses without applying the lesson to Omega itself -- the corpus had the instrument and did not turn it on itself.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 12.8 Net effect on the disposition (before/after table)
rationale_evidence.statement: Summarizes the net effect of the section-12 evidence sweep in a before/after table: in-window senses unchanged at 5; out-of-window senses grow from 1 to 2 (adding Omega-7); Omega_a/b/c goes from 'never defined' to defined 08-28 15:01 with 238 having altered Omega-c's recorded fate; governance goes from 'no act' to GN-09+D-R27 found (though not covering Omega-1/2/3); prior art on the collision goes from 'none found' to TG-15 and C-06 found; the Omega-1xOmega-2 HOMONYM finding remains STILL NEW since Omega-1 appears in none of TG-15's four senses; Omega-1xOmega-3 remains UNDECIDABLE, now with a refuted attribution attached; the G-21 gate remains open with its constraint unchanged, now double-sourced.

rationale_evidence.anchor: §7 · C-06 — a local ruling against COMBINING, not a global verdict on Ω ... C-06 adjudicates that two HOMONYMS must not be combined. It does NOT rule that Ω is contradictory. ... the corpus independently reaches the same separation five days later ... CORROBORATIVE, and by §9 this counts as two lineages, not two documents.
rationale_evidence.statement: Re-examines the corpus's own C-06 'TRUE CONTRADICTION' ruling (Omega=Knowledge Space vs Omega:W->O) verbatim, identifying it addresses specifically Omega-7 vs Omega-2, contradicting the 031 non-identifiability result, is a mathematical+semantic (set vs function) type incompatibility, concerns objects G-22 already classed DISTINCT, and crucially is BOUNDED/conditional ('combining them WOULD make...') rather than a global verdict. Concludes C-06 rules only that two homonyms must not be COMBINED, not that Omega itself is contradictory. Notes the corpus independently reaches the identical separation five days later via Omega-B's explicit rejection of Omega=K, in a different lane, with no citation between the two -- classified as two independent (CORROBORATIVE) lineages rather than a single duplicated finding.

rationale_evidence.anchor: §12 · Continuity with apparatus loss — the Ω instance, and it is sharper than 026's ... A gap was opened for an object the corpus had DEFINED THREE DAYS EARLIER — and then closed by 'recovering' it. ... apparatus never left the corpus — only the working set — and its re-discovery was recorded as a gap closure.
rationale_evidence.statement: Traces a precise sequence: 031 defines Omega:W->O boxed (08-28 10:22) -> a 155-file silence -> Omega returns (08-29) -> step_251 cites it unattributed (08-30) -> a NEW GAP is explicitly opened ('Gap 1: (W,Omega) referent layer', 08-31 19:03) -> the same gap is closed hours later by 'recovering' the Sanjaya layer (08-31 19:52, G3->G5) -> a claim that 'the earlier claim that the verification lane lacked an entire observation/referent layer is no longer valid' (08-31 19:40) -> Omega-A's document frames this as resolving 'a structural omission discovered in D285-6' (08-31 20:11). Concludes a gap was opened for an object the corpus had already defined three days earlier, then closed by 'recovering' it -- the corpus does not record this as a loss, it records it as a discovery. Contrasts this with G-12's 026 mechanism ('continuity declared, apparatus not carried'): here, the apparatus never left the corpus at all, only the ACTIVE WORKING SET did, and its re-discovery was mislabeled a gap closure -- two distinct mechanisms in one family, recorded as evidence not generalized into a law.

rationale_evidence.anchor: §10 · Mathematical audit (Ω-A PROVEN function W→O, Ω-B UNKNOWN never typed, Ω-C PROVEN as a set/UNKNOWN membership, Ω-D contradictory within one file) ... No TYPE-CONSTRAINED value was promoted to PROVEN. §11 · DDD audit ... Four bounded-context candidates, one glyph, zero context mappings.
rationale_evidence.statement: Mathematical audit: Omega-A is PROVEN as function W->O; Omega-B is UNKNOWN, never typed at all; Omega-C is PROVEN as a finite set but its membership is UNKNOWN; Omega-D is contradictory within one file (measure space and element set simultaneously). Notes no type-constrained value in this audit was ever promoted to PROVEN status. DDD audit assigns each Omega sense to a distinct bounded context (Omega-A observation/referent layer -- map reality to observation; Omega-B epistemic framing/Gita lens -- situate a finite state against a horizon, explicitly Omega!=K and Omega!=God per the corpus; Omega-C kernel -- delimit permitted operations; Omega-D Gita-derived mathematics -- integration domain/state set), concluding four bounded-context candidates share one glyph with zero context mappings between them.

sources.note: The formal 'REFINED-STEP-290 -- OPERATION SEMANTICS' research-mandate proposal (S2285): a narrowly-scoped operation-semantics research charter with 13 non-goals, a nine-class evidence classification, and an anti-overclaiming table.

rows.anchor: Step 290 must define what it means for a KnowledgeOS operation to be semantically valid, without prematurely selecting the final operation set, kernel state, equality relation, or implementation. ... Step 290 answers a narrower question than 'what is the KnowledgeOS kernel?': What does it mean for an operation to act upon KnowledgeOS state? ... Sem(o,K) must be investigated before assuming delta(K,o)=K' is sufficient.
rows.statement: Proposes REFINED-STEP-290 — OPERATION SEMANTICS as a research mandate (depends on Steps 261, 285-289; authority: research derives, governance ratifies) whose purpose is strictly narrower than defining the kernel: establish what it means for an operation to act on KnowledgeOS state, formalized as investigating Sem(o,K) before assuming delta(K,o)=K' is sufficient, and considering whether operations require a richer model (events, assertions, observations, evidence, provenance, policy, authority, rejection, retraction, contradiction, history, time, external effects).

rows.anchor: Step 290 MUST NOT: select the final KnowledgeOS kernel; declare (A,R) to be the kernel; resolve the equality decision problem; decide whether Pi in equiv; define the final observation model; introduce new primitives; promote philosophical concepts into architecture; select a final operation registry; declare delta total; assume operations are deterministic; assume every operation changes K; assume every operation is reversible; resolve Governance questions by mathematical argument. operation semantics != operation registry != implementation.
rows.statement: Lists 13 explicit non-goals bounding the proposed Step 290 (must not select the final kernel, declare (A,R) the kernel, resolve the equality decision problem, decide Pi-in-equiv, define the final observation model, introduce new primitives, promote philosophy into architecture, select a final operation registry, declare delta total, assume determinism/universality-of-change/reversibility, or resolve governance questions mathematically), summarized as operation semantics != operation registry != implementation.

rows.anchor: Step 290 inherits: Step 261 -- kernel cannot be finally selected while equality/observation/operation contracts unresolved. Step 285 -- K_t -pi_K-> (A,R) is an established semantic projection, operational interpretation unestablished. Step 287 -- four distinct state-level relations (=, equiv, approx, cong_lambda) with unresolved decision procedures. Step 288 -- equality OPEN, identity partially specified, operation/transformation semantics OPEN. Step 290 may reason about operations without closing these blockers.
rows.statement: Enumerates the inherited unresolved conditions Step 290 must carry forward without closing: Step 261's kernel-selection gate; Step 285's semantic projection K_t-pi_K->(A,R) with unestablished operational interpretation; Step 287's four unresolved state-level relations (=, equiv, approx, cong_lambda); Step 288's open equality/identity/operation/transformation semantics -- an explicit worked instance of the 'inherited gates' discipline discussed elsewhere in this batch (S2282/S2283).

rows.anchor: Level 1 -- Operation identity: what makes o_1=o_2 true? candidates: identifier, type, version, parameters, semantic specification, authority, provenance. Level 2 -- Operation semantics: what does the operation mean? [[o]](K)=K' or [[o]](K,O)=K' or [[o]](K,I)=(K',E). Level 3 -- Operation execution: how is that semantic meaning implemented (database transaction, event emission, workflow transition, API call, human decision, AI inference)? Implementation must not be used to define semantics. identity != semantics != execution.
rows.statement: Requires three levels to remain formally separate: Level 1 Operation identity (what makes o_1=o_2 true -- candidates identifier/type/version/parameters/semantic spec/authority/provenance, none chosen without evidence); Level 2 Operation semantics (what the operation means, candidate denotation forms [[o]](K)=K', [[o]](K,O)=K', or [[o]](K,I)=(K',E) with E for emitted effects); Level 3 Operation execution (how meaning is implemented -- database transaction, event emission, workflow transition, API call, human decision, AI inference) -- with the rule that implementation must never be used to define semantics: identity != semantics != execution.

rows.anchor: Test whether K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t) or K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t,I_t) or (K_{t+1},E_t)=delta(K_t,o_t,I_t). ... an operation may: change state; emit an event; create evidence; invoke an external system; fail; be rejected; produce no state change; produce an auditable record despite rejection.
rows.statement: Poses three competing candidate operation-signature models to test against the corpus: the plain K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t); the input-explicit K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t,I_t); and the effect-producing (K_{t+1},E_t)=delta(K_t,o_t,I_t) -- motivated by the observation that an operation may change state, emit an event, create evidence, invoke an external system, fail, be rejected, produce no state change, or produce an auditable record despite rejection, none of which the plain signature can express.
missing: selection among the three signature models

rows.anchor: Query q:K->R no state mutation. State transformation delta:K->K'. Observation acquisition a:W->O. Assertion creation alpha:(O,E,C)->A. Governance operation g:K x Pi -> K'. External effect e:K->(K',X). These are candidate classes only. The research must determine whether they are actually needed.
rows.statement: Proposes six candidate semantic operation classes to test, not assume: Query (q:K->R, no mutation), State transformation (delta:K->K'), Observation acquisition (a:W->O), Assertion creation (alpha:(O,E,C)->A), Governance operation (g:K x Pi -> K'), External effect (e:K->(K',X)) -- explicitly candidate only, needing independent justification.

rows.anchor: Pre(o,K)=false means: operation rejected; operation invalid; operation has no effect; operation generates an event; operation produces a failure state; operation is itself recorded. Do not collapse these cases. ... Post(o,K,K') necessary/sufficient/deterministic/observable/verifiable? Pre(o,K) and Execute(o,K) => Post(o,K,K') must be tested against the corpus rather than assumed.
rows.statement: Requires precondition-failure semantics not be collapsed into one meaning: Pre(o,K)=false could mean the operation is rejected, invalid, has no effect, generates an event, produces a failure state, or is itself recorded -- six distinguishable outcomes. Postcondition semantics Post(o,K,K') must be separately tested for necessity, sufficiency, determinism, observability, and verifiability, with Pre(o,K) and Execute(o,K) => Post(o,K,K') tested against the corpus, not assumed.
missing: resolution among the six Pre=false interpretations

rows.anchor: Test whether Reject(o,K) is semantically different from Fail(o,K) and from NoOp(o,K). Rejected != Execution failure != Successful operation with unchanged state. This should be cross-checked with the existing Reject <-> I-12 <-> Article 8 governance question. Step 290 must not resolve that governance question.
rows.statement: Requires a dedicated investigation distinguishing Reject(o,K), Fail(o,K), and NoOp(o,K) as three semantically distinct outcomes (rejected != execution failure != successful operation with unchanged state), explicitly cross-referenced to but not resolving the existing Reject<->I-12<->Article 8 governance question.

rows.anchor: Investigate whether the semantics require delta(K,o)=K' uniquely, or whether delta(K,o) in {K_1',K_2',...} is possible. If nondeterminism exists, distinguish: environmental nondeterminism, observational uncertainty, policy ambiguity, concurrent operations, genuinely nondeterministic semantics. Do not confuse epistemic uncertainty with mathematical nondeterminism. ... For each candidate operation class investigate delta(delta(K,o),o)=delta(K,o). If false, determine why. Do not assume all KnowledgeOS operations should be idempotent.
rows.statement: Requires testing whether delta(K,o)=K' is unique (deterministic) or genuinely multi-valued, distinguishing five possible sources of apparent nondeterminism (environmental, observational uncertainty, policy ambiguity, concurrency, genuine nondeterminism) and warning against confusing epistemic uncertainty with mathematical nondeterminism. Separately requires testing idempotence per operation class (delta(delta(K,o),o)=delta(K,o)) without assuming universal idempotence, illustrated by five example operations (record observation, approve assertion, withdraw assertion, replay event, publish artifact) that may have radically different algebraic properties.

rows.anchor: Investigate o_2 circ o_1 and determine when composition exists. Is composition associative? partial? deterministic? provenance-preserving? policy-preserving? Do not assume an operation algebra exists merely because composition is mathematically convenient. ... Investigate whether o_1 circ o_2 = o_2 circ o_1 is meaningful. Potential causes of non-commutation: shared state, conflicting assertions, governance ordering, provenance, temporal dependency.
rows.statement: Requires investigating operation composition o_2 o o_1 for existence conditions, associativity, partiality, determinism, provenance-preservation, and policy-preservation, warning against assuming an operation algebra exists merely because composition is mathematically convenient. Separately requires investigating commutation o_1 o o_2 = o_2 o o_1, with five candidate causes of non-commutation (shared state, conflicting assertions, governance ordering, provenance, temporal dependency), noting history may matter even when final content looks identical.

rows.anchor: Step 290 must distinguish replay from re-execution. If an operation is replayed, is KnowledgeOS reconstructing a historical state or executing the operation again? Replay(H) -> K_t versus Execute(o,K_t) -> K_{t+1}. This connects directly to the Step-285 finding that K_t is replay-capable. ... test whether Pi(K') supseteq Pi(K) is required. But do not assume monotonicity. Withdrawal/retraction may change provenance semantics. Investigate instead Pi' = P_Pi(K,o) as a candidate provenance transformation.
rows.statement: Requires distinguishing replay (Replay(H)->K_t, reconstructing a historical state) from re-execution (Execute(o,K_t)->K_{t+1}, executing again), connecting to Step 285's replay-capability finding for K_t. Requires testing provenance preservation without assuming monotonicity (Pi(K') supseteq Pi(K) is NOT assumed, since withdrawal/retraction may change provenance semantics), proposing instead a general candidate provenance transformation Pi' = P_Pi(K,o).

rows.anchor: Test Operation != Event and determine whether Operation -> Event or Event -> Operation or neither. The corpus already contains both primitives Event, Action and therefore Step 290 must not silently merge them. ... Operation != Action? Operation = semantic transition specification, Action = something performed, Event = something that occurred/is recorded. But this is only a hypothesis.
rows.statement: Requires a formal audit that Operation != Event, testing the direction of any implication (Operation->Event, Event->Operation, or neither) without silently merging the corpus's existing Event and Action primitives. Separately proposes (as hypothesis only) Operation != Action, with a candidate three-way distinction: Operation = semantic transition specification, Action = something performed, Event = something that occurred/is recorded.

rows.anchor: Test whether Policy is: part of operation identity; an operation precondition; an external constraint; an input; part of semantic interpretation; provenance; none of these. This must remain connected to Step 287 Decision 3: Pi in equiv? but must not answer that decision prematurely. ... Separate authority to execute from authority recorded by execution. An operation may record AuthorityRef without creating authority. recording authority != granting authority, but the exact operation semantics remain open.
rows.statement: Poses seven candidate roles for Policy relative to an operation (part of identity, a precondition, an external constraint, an input, part of semantic interpretation, provenance, or none of these) connected to but not prematurely resolving Step 287 Decision 3 (is Pi in the equality relation?). Separately requires separating 'authority to execute' from 'authority recorded by execution' -- an operation may record an AuthorityRef without creating authority, restating the anti-regress principle 'recording authority != granting authority' while leaving the exact operation semantics open.

rows.anchor: Mathematical test programme: Identity, Domain, Partiality, Determinism, No-op, Idempotence, Composition, Associativity, Commutation, Replay, Provenance, Rejection, Failure, Observation, Event -- 15 properties each with a specific question. Every PASS must state exactly what object was tested. No 'operations are associative' unless the operation domain and composition operation have actually been defined.
rows.statement: Specifies a mandatory 15-property mathematical test programme (identity, domain, partiality, determinism, no-op, idempotence, composition, associativity, commutation, replay, provenance, rejection, failure, observation, event), each with a precise question, and a rigor rule: every PASS must state exactly what object was tested -- forbidding vague claims like 'operations are associative' unless the operation domain and composition operation have actually been defined.

rows.anchor: The DDD audit must determine whether Operation is: Entity, Value Object, Domain Service, Command, Domain Event, Policy, Specification, Process, or merely a mathematical abstraction. Command != Operation unless the bounded context explicitly establishes the correspondence. Likewise Domain Event != Operation. DDD terminology must not be used as a substitute for semantic definition.
rows.statement: Requires a DDD audit testing whether Operation maps to Entity, Value Object, Domain Service, Command, Domain Event, Policy, Specification, Process, or merely a mathematical abstraction, with an explicit warning that Command != Operation and Domain Event != Operation unless the bounded context establishes the correspondence -- DDD terminology must not substitute for semantic definition.

rows.anchor: Critical distinction: Operation Semantics != Transformation Semantics. Operation semantics answer: what does this operation mean and under what conditions is it applicable? Transformation semantics answer: given an applicable operation, exactly how does state change? Therefore Step 290 may establish Applicable(K,o) without establishing delta(K,o)=K'. This is likely the most important boundary of the entire step.
rows.statement: States what the document calls likely the most important boundary of the entire step: Operation Semantics != Transformation Semantics -- operation semantics answer 'what does this operation mean and when is it applicable' (formalized as establishing Applicable(K,o)), while transformation semantics answer 'given an applicable operation, exactly how does state change' (delta(K,o)=K'); Step 290 may establish the former without establishing the latter.

rows.anchor: Evidence classification: CORPUS, DERIVED, EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED, CORROBORATED, HYPOTHESIS, NORMATIVE, OPEN, BLOCKED, REFUTED -- nine classes, each conclusion gets exactly one. Do not use 'established' merely because a mathematical model is elegant. ... Mandatory anti-overclaiming table: 'delta is the transformation function' -> 'delta is a candidate transformation notation'; 'Operation is a Command' -> 'Command correspondence is under investigation'; ... 'Buddhi is the kernel' -> 'Buddhi is a philosophical lens for discrimination'.
rows.statement: Requires a nine-class evidence classification (CORPUS, DERIVED, EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED, CORROBORATED, HYPOTHESIS, NORMATIVE, OPEN, BLOCKED, REFUTED), one class per conclusion, warning against calling something 'established' merely because it is elegant. Mandates an anti-overclaiming table mapping eight tempting overstatements to permitted weaker forms (e.g. 'delta is the transformation function' -> 'delta is a candidate transformation notation'; 'Buddhi is the kernel' -> 'Buddhi is a philosophical lens for discrimination').

rows.anchor: Does Step 290 close any Step-261 blocker? The default answer must be: Only if the evidence independently satisfies the corresponding gate. Do not declare Step 261 closed merely because Step 290 produces a formal operation model. formal operation model != canonical kernel. ... Expected outcome space: A Functional transition model, B Relation-based semantics, C Effect-producing semantics, D Event-sourced semantics, E Hybrid, F Insufficient evidence -- operation semantics remain under-specified. No outcome may be selected because it is architecturally attractive.
rows.statement: Requires an end-of-step Step-261 gate audit defaulting to NO closure unless evidence independently satisfies the gate (formal operation model != canonical kernel). Defines an open six-outcome space for the whole step with no predetermined winner: (A) functional transition model delta:K x O harpoonup K, (B) relation-based semantics R_o(K,K'), (C) effect-producing semantics delta:K x O -> K x E, (D) event-sourced semantics K_t=Replay(E_0:t), (E) a hybrid structure over K,O,E,Pi,P,A, or (F) the honest finding that operation semantics remain under-specified -- explicitly forbidding selecting an outcome merely because it is architecturally attractive.

rows.anchor: Step 290 establishes what must be true for an operation to have semantics; it does not by itself establish the final KnowledgeOS operation set or kernel. Operation semantics != operation implementation != canonical kernel. ... I would not put Observation research inside Step 290. Observation is a separate conceptual dependency and should be investigated as its own controlled step. ... 285 Canonical State Reconciliation -> 286 Philosophical-Source Hypothesis Programme -> 287 Equality/Identity/Observability -> 288 Equality Closure Audit -> 289 Operations inventory -> 290 Operation Semantics -> 291 Observation Semantics -> 292 Dimension -> 293 Statement -> ...
rows.statement: States the final boundary: Step 290 establishes only what must be true for an operation to have semantics, never the final operation set or kernel (operation semantics != operation implementation != canonical kernel). Recommends against embedding Observation research inside Step 290 -- Observation is a separate conceptual dependency needing its own controlled step -- proposing a renumbered nine-step programme: 285 Canonical State Reconciliation, 286 Philosophical-Source Hypothesis Programme, 287 Equality/Identity/Observability, 288 Equality Closure Audit, 289 Operations inventory/candidate space, 290 Operation Semantics, 291 Observation Semantics, 292 Dimension, 293 Statement, continuing onward -- with Step 261 remaining an overarching gate throughout, not a superseded historical step. This renumbering directly creates the step-number collision with the corpus's separately-numbered 'Step 290 -- N-1 Adjudication,' per the filename's own framing.

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: our programme has now moved from *trying to discover the kernel directly* to **reconstructing the ontology and operation semantics that could justify a kernel**. ... $$\text{Operation Semantics}\prec\text{Operation Algebra}\prec\text{Transformation Algebra}\prec\text{Kernel Selection}$$
rows.statement: States the programme's fundamental reordering: from trying to discover the kernel directly to reconstructing the ontology and operation semantics that could justify a kernel, formalized as a strict precedence chain Operation Semantics precedes Operation Algebra precedes Transformation Algebra precedes Kernel Selection.

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: "This is the correct conceptual architecture." No. At this stage it is a **candidate conceptual model**. Likewise: "Buddhi as the discrimination mechanism" should remain a **philosophical hypothesis / modelling interpretation**, not an architectural fact. ... Conceptual model = research hypothesis, not: Conceptual model = architecture.
rows.statement: Explicitly rejects an HPA assessment's over-strong claims ('this is the correct conceptual architecture'; 'the kernel with Buddhi as the discrimination mechanism'), downgrading them to a candidate conceptual model and a philosophical hypothesis/modelling interpretation respectively -- Conceptual model = research hypothesis, never = architecture, until independent derivation and governance ratify it.

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: $$O_t^{candidate}=(x,t,c,s)$$ because each component raises unresolved questions. ... Observation != Interpretation must be tested rather than merely asserted. ... it prevents us from smuggling unresolved concepts into the operation algebra.
rows.statement: Downgrades the proposed Observation model O_t=(x,t,c,s) to O_t^candidate, since each component (what x actually is: signal/value/event/proposition/measurement/representation; whether t is intrinsic or metadata; whether c is observation-internal or provenance; whether s is mandatory) raises unresolved questions, and Observation != Interpretation must be tested rather than merely asserted -- explicitly framed as preventing unresolved concepts from being smuggled into the operation algebra.
missing: resolution of each of the four O_t component questions

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: before we can define delta(K,o) we must know what o actually is. ... what counts as an operation; what its input state is; what its input object is; what output state means; whether it is deterministic; whether it is partial; what invariants it preserves; what identity it uses; what provenance it creates; whether it is reversible; whether it is monotone; whether it is governed; whether rejection is itself an operation or an outcome.
rows.statement: Argues that defining a transformation delta(K,o) presupposes knowing what o actually is, enumerating thirteen prior questions that must be answered before delta can even be well-defined (what counts as an operation; input state/object; output meaning; determinism; partiality; preserved invariants; identity used; provenance created; reversibility; monotonicity; governance; whether rejection is an operation or an outcome).

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: Step 290 establishes the semantic contract of an operation independently of the final operation inventory. It determines the carrier, input/output meaning, preconditions, postconditions, identity effects, provenance effects, partiality, determinism, composition requirements, and invariant obligations ... It does not select the canonical operation set ... $$o:(K,I,C,G)\rightharpoonup(K',E)$$
rows.statement: Redefines Step 290's mission precisely: establish the semantic contract of an operation (carrier, input/output meaning, preconditions/postconditions, identity/provenance effects, partiality, determinism, composition requirements, invariant obligations) independently of and prior to selecting the final operation inventory, formalized as a deliberately carrier-open partial function o:(K,I,C,G) -harpoon-> (K',E), itself explicitly only a candidate meta-model, not a ratified contract.
missing: ratification of the carriers K,I,C,G and the candidate meta-model itself

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: Step-288 result actually makes Step 290 **more constrained**, not less. ... equality remains OPEN. ... Step 290 cannot assume K1=_equiv K2 or K1~K2 or K1=K2 as interchangeable. ... an operation cannot casually be specified as o(K)=K' and then say that the operation "preserves knowledge." Preserves **under which equality?**
rows.statement: Argues Step 288's finding that equality remains open makes Step 290 MORE constrained, not less: Step 290 cannot treat semantic equality, observational approximate-equality, and structural equality as interchangeable, and any claim that an operation 'preserves knowledge' is meaningless until the specific equality relation intended is named.

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: $$\text{Identity}\leftrightarrow\text{Equality}\leftrightarrow\text{Operation Semantics}$$ ... What does it mean to say: "operation o did not change the knowledge state"? It could mean: K'=K structurally, or: K' equiv K semantically, or: K' approx_X K observationally, or: K' cong_lambda K provenance-sensitively. These are **different claims**.
rows.statement: Introduces the Identity-Equality-Operation-Semantics triangle: determining whether an operation changed the knowledge state requires specifying which of at least four distinct relations is meant (structural equality K'=K, semantic equality K'=_equiv K, observational approximate-equality K'~_X K, or provenance-sensitive equality K'=_lambda K) -- these are genuinely different claims, so Step 290 must prohibit unqualified 'operation X preserves the state' statements.

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: It does **not** provide O. It does not define delta. It does not prove Buddhi=Discriminate. Instead it gives conceptual lenses that may generate hypotheses. ... corroboration != derivation. ... philosophical objection -> candidate missing concept rather than: philosophical objection -> new primitive.
rows.statement: Clarifies the Gita/Cavell philosophical-lens role: it provides neither the operator set O, nor the transformation delta, nor a proof that Buddhi=Discriminate -- only conceptual lenses generating candidate hypotheses (Karma -> action/result hypothesis, Buddhi -> discrimination hypothesis, Vairagya -> outcome-independence hypothesis); reaffirms corroboration != derivation and reframes a philosophical objection as producing a candidate missing concept, never directly a new primitive.

rows.anchor: $$Observation\rightarrow Dimension\rightarrow Statement\rightarrow Value\rightarrow Knowledge\rightarrow\cdots$$ ... It is not yet proven that this is the **ontology's dependency order**. It is: **current research dependency hypothesis**. ... every transition should be testable.
rows.statement: Downgrades the 20-concept Observation->Dimension->Statement->Value->Knowledge dependency sequence from an established ontological dependency order to a current research dependency hypothesis, noting research may later discover e.g. Evidence precedes Observation or that Statement is not an independent object at all -- every transition in the sequence must remain independently testable.

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th

rows.statement: Proposes a nine-layer research-programme architecture (Philosophical Lenses -> Research Hypotheses -> Conceptual/Epistemic Model -> Mathematical Model -> Operation Semantics -> Transformation delta -> Operational Kernel -> Implementation -> Governance), judged substantially better than starting research directly with the kernel.

rows.anchor: Established: K_t is the ratified KnowledgeOS state anchor ... Equality has multiple non-interchangeable forms. Equality is not yet operationally closed. ... Bounded: ... Hypotheses: O_t=(x,t,c,s); Buddhi as discrimination; the four-level model; the 20-concept dependency sequence; Zero as epistemic boundary; any direct Gita->KnowledgeOS mapping. Still open: Observation ontology; Equality procedures; Identity semantics; Operation semantics; Operation registry; Transformation delta; Kernel state; Kernel operation set; Governance decisions.
rows.statement: Produces a four-category status ledger for the whole programme: Established (K_t is the ratified state anchor; its relation to (A,R) is a lossy semantic projection; equality has multiple non-interchangeable forms and is not operationally closed; the Step-261 kernel-selection stop gate remains active; philosophical sources cannot establish architecture; operations require semantic specification before algebraic treatment); Bounded (observational comparison, the equality problem's finite branch set, policy composition's AND-only behaviour, several derivable operation properties); Hypotheses (O_t=(x,t,c,s), Buddhi-as-discrimination, the four-level model, the 20-concept sequence, Zero as epistemic boundary, any direct Gita mapping); Still Open (nine named items: Observation ontology, equality procedures, identity semantics, operation semantics, operation registry, transformation delta, kernel state, kernel operation set, governance decisions).

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: Make it: **"What does it mean for something to be a KnowledgeOS operation?"** Then Step 290 should investigate, at minimum: 1. Operation identity ... 20. Boundary between semantic operation and implementation mechanism. ... Step 290 must derive the semantic requirements for operations; it must not prematurely choose the operations.
rows.statement: States Step 290's redefined guiding question ('what does it mean for something to be a KnowledgeOS operation') and its twenty-item minimum investigation checklist (operation identity, input, carrier, preconditions, postconditions, state transition, partiality, determinism, provenance, event generation, governance/authority effects, the equality needed to state operation properties, composition, idempotence, commutativity, monotonicity, reversibility/retraction, failure/rejection semantics, interaction with K_t/O_t/D_t, and the boundary between semantic operation and implementation mechanism) -- deriving semantic requirements for operations, never prematurely choosing the operations themselves.

rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/brainstorming/phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/prompts/step_290_Yes — **I agree with the direction of th
rows.anchor: the **epistemic status of the entire programme has changed**: $$\text{Architecture-first}\quad\longrightarrow\quad\text{Ontology-first}\quad\longrightarrow\quad\text{Semantics-first}\quad\longrightarrow\quad\text{Algebra}\quad\longrightarrow\quad\text{Architecture}$$ And I think this is the **correct direction**.
rows.statement: States the file's closing bottom-line: the whole programme's epistemic status has shifted from Architecture-first to Ontology-first to Semantics-first to Algebra and only then back to Architecture, endorsed as the correct research direction.

lexical.anchor: Step 290 must define what it means for a KnowledgeOS operation to be semantically valid, without prematurely selecting the final operation set, kernel state, equality relation, or implementation. ... Step 290 answers a narrower question than 'what is the KnowledgeOS kernel?': What does it mean for an operation to act upon KnowledgeOS state? ... Sem(o,K) must be investigated before assuming delta(K,o)=K' is sufficient.

formal.anchor: Level 1 -- Operation identity: what makes o_1=o_2 true? candidates: identifier, type, version, parameters, semantic specification, authority, provenance. Level 2 -- Operation semantics: what does the operation mean? [[o]](K)=K' or [[o]](K,O)=K' or [[o]](K,I)=(K',E). Level 3 -- Operation execution: how is that semantic meaning implemented (database transaction, event emission, workflow transition, API call, human decision, AI inference)? Implementation must not be used to define semantics. identity != semantics != execution.

governance.anchor: Step 290 must define what it means for a KnowledgeOS operation to be semantically valid, without prematurely selecting the final operation set, kernel state, equality relation, or implementation. ... Step 290 answers a narrower question than 'what is the KnowledgeOS kernel?': What does it mean for an operation to act upon KnowledgeOS state? ... Sem(o,K) must be investigated before assuming delta(K,o)=K' is sufficient.

rationale_evidence.anchor: before we can define delta(K,o) we must know what o actually is. ... what counts as an operation; what its input state is; what its input object is; what output state means; whether it is deterministic; whether it is partial; what invariants it preserves; what identity it uses; what provenance it creates; whether it is reversible; whether it is monotone; whether it is governed; whether rejection is itself an operation or an outcome.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues that defining a transformation delta(K,o) presupposes knowing what o actually is, enumerating thirteen prior questions that must be answered before delta can even be well-defined (what counts as an operation; input state/object; output meaning; determinism; partiality; preserved invariants; identity used; provenance created; reversibility; monotonicity; governance; whether rejection is an operation or an outcome).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Step-288 result actually makes Step 290 **more constrained**, not less. ... equality remains OPEN. ... Step 290 cannot assume K1=_equiv K2 or K1~K2 or K1=K2 as interchangeable. ... an operation cannot casually be specified as o(K)=K' and then say that the operation "preserves knowledge." Preserves **under which equality?**
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues Step 288's finding that equality remains open makes Step 290 MORE constrained, not less: Step 290 cannot treat semantic equality, observational approximate-equality, and structural equality as interchangeable, and any claim that an operation 'preserves knowledge' is meaningless until the specific equality relation intended is named.

rows.statement: Corrects an inflated open-gap estimate (~18) to the actual count: 8 DISPOSED (G-02,G-03,G-08,G-14,G-18,G-19,G-20,G-22), 1 SUBSUMED (G-10 into G-22), 1 DEFERRED BY METHOD (G-04), and 12 truly OPEN (G-01,G-05,G-06,G-07,G-09,G-11,G-12,G-15,G-16,G-17,G-21,C-1). Frames this as the third of three independent lanes to diagnose the same self-search-failure defect in itself (citing kernel/research/14-GAP-UPDATE...: 'This is not a failure of the corpus. It is a failure of my search.').
