sources.note: The verification lane's 2026-09-02 self-audit retracting four absence claims from its own prior theory-compatibility series (00/03/05/06) as scope-limited zeros (a probe over 564 of 3,136+ brainstorming files, using glyph-literal patterns over a LaTeX corpus) wrongly reported as theory-wide absences, plus two further corrections (NG-4's transitivity premise; the R_req congruence-conjunct claim), and adopting a standing rule requiring scope-as-fraction, a concept-level synonym search, and a positive control before any future absence claim.

rows.anchor: I measured 18% of one folder and wrote "0 in both lanes" as a property of the theory. ... the patterns were glyph-literal ... The corpus writes mathematics in LaTeX
rows.statement: The theory-compatibility probe covered 564 of 3,136+ brainstorming files (18% of one folder alone) using glyph-literal search patterns (e.g. literal '(Omega,F,P)') against a corpus that writes its mathematics in LaTeX (e.g. '(\Omega,\mathscr G,P)') -- a pattern that cannot find its target regardless of whether the target exists, so any zero from it is meaningless; two independent errors (scope and glyph-literalism) compounded to produce four false absence claims.

rows.anchor: The measurable structure is DEFINED. The probability law is DEFERRED, explicitly and conditionally -- "when uncertainty is probabilistically modeled."
rows.statement: WITHDRAWN: the claim '(Omega,F,P) as a triple: 0 in both lanes.' Re-measured over docs/knowledgeos/: a 'probability space' appears in 134 files, 'measure space' in 20, 'filtration' in 41; and a dated 2026-09-02 definition exists for a Knowledge Space KS=(X,A) (X a space of admissible epistemic configurations, A the sigma-field of admissible epistemic observables) with K_t inducing a measurable compatibility region Gamma(K_t) in A and epistemic information as a filtration F_0 subset F_1 subset ..., with a probability law over (X,A) or over trajectories Omega_K explicitly optional ('when uncertainty is probabilistically modeled'). The measurable structure is defined; only the probability law is deferred -- and this improves rather than undermines the probability document's central claim that typing needs a measurable space while dynamics need a metric.

rows.anchor: Theta is present as A_Q, the adequately scoped alternative space -- a REQUIREMENT of Determine, with an incompleteness result I did not have.
rows.statement: WITHDRAWN: 'Theta has never been raised, unlike P' (the load-bearing claim of theory-compatibility 05 and 06, and the basis for hypothesis DT-H4). A dated 2026-09-02 00:47 document proves Determine(K,Q,EC) requires an adequately scoped alternative space A_Q (boxed: Determination requires an adequately scoped alternative space), and goes further with an incompleteness result the retracting author did not have: pairwise superiority != global determination, demanding a four-way split of Determine into comparative/exclusive/global/insufficiently-scoped. Consequence: DT-H4 is withdrawn (it was named, under a different symbol, five days earlier); the statistical-decision-theory verdict 'structurally compatible, materially empty' is downgraded to 'materially thinner than the frame requires' since A_Q exists even though a loss function and a probability law still do not.

rows.anchor: Dempster's rule needs an independence ASSUMPTION. This corpus returns Unknown by default and demands a policy to discharge it.
rows.statement: WITHDRAWN and INVERTED: 'TG-02's missing independence relation.' A dated 2026-08-27 document (five days before the claim) already defines Independent(e_i,e_j) as a non-Boolean six-component independence evidence vector I(e_i,e_j)=(i_S,i_A,i_P,i_M,i_T,i_C) with conservative rules (a common ancestor forces the result to Unknown, not Independent; different source does not imply independence). This inverts the original conclusion: Dempster's combination rule is blocked not because KnowledgeOS lacks an independence relation, but because the relation it has is present and deliberately refuses to be Boolean, discharging to Unknown by default -- named as a fourth instance of the series' recurring pattern (the external theory assumes something the corpus deliberately refuses).

rows.anchor: A zero is a measurement of a SCOPE and a PATTERN. It is never a property of a theory.
rows.statement: Standing methodological rule adopted for the verification lane after this correction episode: no absence claim may be made without (i) the scope stated as a fraction of the estate, (ii) at least one concept-level synonym search alongside any glyph search, and (iii) a positive control (a term known to be present, to prove the search pattern can match at all).

sources.note: A second, distinct hpa treatment of Chapter 2 (companion to S2255), explicitly framed as a KERNEL-LEVEL REFINEMENT rather than a new layer. Expands K_t=content+interpretation+relationships+epistemic condition (from Arjuna having facts but an incomplete conceptual model). Introduces Reframe(K_t)->K_t' as a legitimate knowledge transformation distinct from accumulation (Knowledge transformation != Knowledge accumulation), motivated by Krishna progressively reframing Arjuna's conceptual model rather than adding facts. Extends Zero's boundary types to five: {unknown,uncertain,contradictory,unqualified,mis-modelled}, the last being a genuinely new category (many facts + wrong model). Gives the chain Knowledge != Decision != Action != Result. Reaffirms N notin K_t (the Knower remains outside the kernel) as an explicit architectural constraint. Proposes final candidate kernel (fraktur K)_t=(K_t,Z_t,M_t,B,O,delta) and a 10-question operator-testing checklist (input/output state, preconditions, invariants, whether it changes K or Sigma, whether it consumes evidence, whether it produces Observation/Event/Action, whether Buddhi is required, mode-dependence) as the concluding research direction.

rows.anchor: K_t = \text{content} + \text{interpretation} + \text{relationships} + \text{epistemic condition}
rows.statement: Expands K_t beyond 'what KnowledgeOS currently knows' to K_t = content + interpretation + relationships + epistemic condition, motivated by Arjuna having substantial information, observations, relationships and beliefs yet remaining unable to determine what to do -- his problem being conceptual gaps and an incomplete model, not merely missing facts. The kernel must operate on the quality and structure of knowledge, not simply its quantity.

rows.anchor: \operatorname{Reframe}(K_t) \rightarrow K'_t ... Knowledge\ transformation \neq Knowledge\ accumulation
rows.statement: From the observation that Krishna progressively reframes Arjuna's conceptual model rather than merely supplying additional information: proposes Reframe(K_t)->K_t' as a potentially fundamental KnowledgeOS operation, where K_t={P_1,P_2,P_3} becomes K_t'={P_1',P_2',P_3'} with the same propositions interpreted under a different conceptual structure -- a knowledge state can change without adding new facts. Hence Knowledge transformation != Knowledge accumulation, added to candidate Buddhi operator set {Compare,Distinguish,Validate,Reject,Reframe,Determine}.

rows.anchor: Z_t = \{ \text{unknown}, \text{uncertain}, \text{contradictory}, \text{unqualified}, \text{mis-modelled} \}
rows.statement: Extends Zero's detected boundary types from missing-data-only to a five-category set Z_t = {unknown, uncertain, contradictory, unqualified, mis-modelled}, with 'mis-modelled' assessed as particularly important and new: a knowledge system may have many facts yet a wrong model (Arjuna's unknowns that he does not recognize as unknowns, more dangerous than ordinary missing information). Hence Zero != missing-data detector only; it becomes an epistemic boundary detector. Gives the chain (K_t,Z_t) --Buddhi--> D_t, and Knowledge != Decision != Action != Result.

lineage_claims.quote: Chapter 2 strengthens the role of Zero.

rows.anchor: Buddhi(K_t,Z_t,M_t) \rightarrow D_t ... Unrecognized ignorance
rows.statement: Extends Buddhi to include the operating mode: Buddhi(K_t,Z_t,M_t)->D_t, giving 'the same Knowledge State can produce different processing trajectories depending on the kernel's operating mode' as a testable hypothesis. Tamas failure mode: kernel encounters Z_t not-empty but behaves as though Z_t=empty, producing unrecognized ignorance; Rajas failure mode: continuous action Action_1->Action_2->Action_3 without sufficient discrimination -- the kernel needs self-regulation, connecting Chapter 6's discipline material to kernel architecture rather than mere commentary.

rows.anchor: \mathcal N\notin K_t ... The kernel is therefore not the Ātman.
rows.statement: Explicitly preserves and reaffirms N notin K_t (the Knower is not inside the current knowledge state) in the combined KOS_t=(K_t,Z_t,B_t,M_t,O_t,delta) model: N -> Kernel -> K_t but N notin K_t; the kernel is not the Atman. The mind/kernel analogy is useful because the kernel performs functions the philosophical model attributes to mind/buddhi, but the analogy must not become an ontological claim.

rows.anchor: What is the smallest algebra of operations required for this kernel to reproduce the epistemic dynamics identified across Chapters 2–18?
rows.statement: Proposes stopping independent chapter analysis and instead deriving the smallest algebra of operations O_K={o_1,...,o_n} required to reproduce the epistemic dynamics identified across Chapters 2-18, testing each operator against 10 questions: input state, output state, preconditions, invariants, whether it changes K, whether it changes Sigma, whether it consumes evidence, whether it produces an Observation/Event/Action, whether Buddhi is required, whether the operator is mode-dependent. Explicitly framed as achievable without letting the Gita dictate the architecture: the Gita supplies the hypothesis, mathematics/DDD/the existing corpus determine whether the operator belongs.

sources.note: Book chapter III.3's ratified content: the time-indexed knowledge state K_t over eight primitives (Entity, State, Event, Observation, Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action), graded TESTED-within-scope; the full reduction derivation from a seven-family stratification to the frozen eight-tuple; per-primitive formal definitions; the derived-structure-layer equations (Evidence, Claim, Identity, Provenance, Uncertainty, Authority, Decision, Outcome as typed structure, not new primitives); PF-2 taught in place (reconstructable argument, but completeness/minimality/uniqueness explicitly not established); and a worked primitive-mis-typing failure case (generic RelatedTo licensing causal hallucination).

rows.anchor: K_{t+1} = Learn( K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t )... the source states the decision and world equations (A_t = Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t); S_{t+1} = F(S_t, A_t, U_t)), keeping three evolutions -- of knowledge, of choices, of the world -- as three different functions.
rows.statement: States the knowledge state's time-indexed dynamics as three separate evolution functions: K_{t+1}=Learn(K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t) for knowledge, A_t=Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t) for choices, and S_{t+1}=F(S_t, A_t, U_t) for the world -- kept as three distinct functions, with time-indexing meaning there is no bare "the knowledge," only knowledge-as-of-t.

rows.anchor: CORE: Entity, State, Event, Observation / EPISTEMIC: Evidence, Claim, Uncertainty / SEMANTIC:... / RELATIONAL:... / GOVERNANCE:... / OPERATIONAL:... / EVOLUTION:... Then, family by family, the source interrogates each concept -- is this primitive, or constructible? -- and most collapse... What survives... K = (E, S, T, O, P, R, Pi, A)
rows.statement: Reproduces the source's reduction derivation from an initial seven-family stratification (Core/Epistemic/Semantic/Relational/Governance/Operational/Evolution) to the frozen eight-tuple candidate kernel K=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Pi,A) -- entities, states, temporal/event structure, observations, propositions, typed relations, policies, actions -- by showing most non-core concepts (Evidence, Claim, Identity, Provenance, Causality/Dependency, Uncertainty, Authority/Decision, Outcome, Learning/Revision/Drift) individually reduce to typed structure over the four cores plus the four surviving structure-carriers (Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action).

Uncertainty = epistemic annotation U(C) (probabilistic OR not -- 49.10's Probability != EpistemicConfidence)... Authority = governance structure over decisions (Authority(actor, d))... resist inventing primitives -- the reduction's whole yield is that richer notions are TYPED STRUCTURE
rows.statement: Lists the derived-structure layer -- the equations by which richer concepts are expressed as typed structure over the eight primitives rather than as new primitives themselves (Evidence=QualifiedObservation; Claim=Proposition; Identity=EntityIdentityRelation; Provenance=TypedDependencyRelation; Uncertainty=epistemic annotation U(C), explicitly not assumed probabilistic -- Probability != EpistemicConfidence; Authority=governance structure over decisions; Decision=structure over K,S,Policy with Proposal kept distinct from AuthorizedDecision; Outcome=observed consequence of Action; Learning/Revision/Drift=evolution structure) and states the modelling discipline this yields: resist inventing new primitives, since typed structure can be checked/queried/governed in ways ad-hoc primitives cannot.

rows.anchor: stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (49.78-49.89... What the argument does not and cannot claim, and the source itself refuses to claim: completeness... minimality... and uniqueness... The source's own word is the governing one: a candidate mathematical kernel.
rows.statement: Teaches PF-2 in place at its exact strength: the eight-primitive reduction argument is RECONSTRUCTABLE, stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (each attempting to express a rich concept in Structure(primitives) and failing the kernel if it cannot be done) plus Step 050's fifty-attack consistency audit; but completeness (no needed concept will ever fail to reduce), minimality (no seven-element basis would suffice -- the source concedes Entity is "arguably" Identity+State, kept for DDD-pragmatic reasons), and uniqueness (no alternative basis exists) remain explicitly NOT ESTABLISHED, matching the source's own characterization of it as a "candidate" kernel and a design result, not a theorem.
missing: proof of completeness, minimality, and uniqueness of the eight-primitive basis

rows.anchor: Collapse the typed relation set into a single generic RelatedTo(A, B) and semantics die: an AI consumer, seeing RelatedTo everywhere, infers RelatedTo => Causes -- recreating "one of the fundamental problems we eliminated in Step 43." One typed set, seven meanings; one generic edge, license to hallucinate causality.
rows.statement: Reproduces the source's own worked failure case for mis-typing the Relation primitive: collapsing the seven typed relations (Supports, DependsOn, Causes, Identifies, MapsTo, Contradicts, Precedes) into a single generic RelatedTo(A,B) edge causes an AI consumer to infer RelatedTo implies Causes, recreating a causal-hallucination failure mode the architecture had previously eliminated; extended to the election running example (DerivedFrom(wireSummary,wireReport) and Supports blurred into RelatedTo would let a derived summary quietly become a second independent witness) as the same dependency failure seen at the primitive-typing layer.
invariants: relations must remain typed, never collapsed to a generic RelatedTo

sources.note: A corpus-integrity finding from Step 289's hidden-order propagation audit: step-060 ('Epistemic Algebra and Knowledge State Ordering') proves the semilattice laws hold only for a restricted merge operator (PureClaimSetUnion, 60.39-41) and explicitly refuses to generalize this to the full knowledge state K (60.42, 60.71: 'we cannot yet assert KnowledgeOS is a semilattice'), yet five separate verification-lane artifacts (KNOWLEDGE-STATE-ALGEBRA.md, THEORY-CLOSURE-AUDIT.md, KNOWLEDGE-STATE-FINAL-AUDIT.md, step_282_theory-closure-decision.md, POLICY-EQUALITY-AND-COMPOSITION.md) assert (K,merge,empty-set) IS a join-semilattice for K generally -- an F5-error-class overclaim (since a join-semilattice structure induces a K-order) combining scope loss, verdict inversion, and an unclassified claim riding beside a genuinely proven Policy-level result. Independently refuted by executed evidence that retraction/withdrawal shrinks the state, contradicting the monotone-growth claim the semilattice framing implies.

rows.anchor: **`step-060` — *Epistemic Algebra and Knowledge State Ordering*:** ... §60.42 ... *"This works for `PureClaimSetUnion`. KnowledgeOS does more than set union… **Therefore the real merge operator may not satisfy the semilattice laws**"* ... §60.71 ... *"Does knowledge form a lattice? **Not proven.** … **we cannot yet assert: KnowledgeOS is a semilattice**"*
rows.statement: Introduces step-060 ('Epistemic Algebra and Knowledge State Ordering') as the actual corpus source on whether knowledge forms a semilattice/lattice: it proves the semilattice laws PASS only for a restricted operator, PureClaimSetUnion (60.39-41), explicitly warns the real merge operator does more than set union so 'the real merge operator may not satisfy the semilattice laws' (60.42), and concludes at 60.71 'not proven ... we cannot yet assert: KnowledgeOS is a semilattice.' This is the corpus's own refusal of the very claim later found to be asserted elsewhere without qualification.

assumptions.statement: the semilattice laws hold for PureClaimSetUnion specifically

rows.anchor: ### Five verification-lane artifacts assert it anyway ... *"`(𝕂, merge, ∅)` is a **join**-semilattice — **adding knowledge only grows the state**"* ... $$\boxed{\text{Asserting } (\mathbb K, merge, \emptyset) \text{ is a join-semilattice IS asserting a } K\textbf{-ORDER}.}$$
rows.statement: Discovers that five separate verification-lane artifacts (KNOWLEDGE-STATE-ALGEBRA.md:89, THEORY-CLOSURE-AUDIT.md:149, KNOWLEDGE-STATE-FINAL-AUDIT.md:29, step_282_theory-closure-decision.md:219, and POLICY-EQUALITY-AND-COMPOSITION.md:73) all assert (K,merge,empty-set) IS a join-semilattice for the full knowledge-state space K, directly contradicting step-060's own explicit refusal of that generalization. Notes formally that asserting a join-semilattice structure on K is itself asserting a K-order (since a join-semilattice induces a partial order K_A <= K_B iff K_A join K_B = K_B), making this instance of the F5-error-class (Sigma/K-order conflation) rather than a mere wording issue.
invariants: a join-semilattice structure induces a partial order

lineage_claims.target: step-060's explicit refusal to assert a semilattice structure for K generally
lineage_claims.quote: §60.71 ... cannot yet assert: KnowledgeOS is a semilattice ... Five verification-lane artifacts assert it anyway

rows.anchor: **Three separate defects:** 1. **Scope loss.** ... 2. **Verdict inversion.** `060.71` says *"cannot yet assert"*; the artifacts assert. 3. ⚠️ **`POLICY-EQUALITY-AND-COMPOSITION` §3 states it as a *"pleasing duality"* — an aesthetic aside ... An unclassified `K`-order claim rode in beside a proven `Policy` one.**
rows.statement: Diagnoses three distinct defects in the semilattice overclaim: (1) scope loss -- 060's result holds only for PureClaimSetUnion, but the five artifacts drop that restriction; (2) verdict inversion -- 060.71 explicitly says 'cannot yet assert', while the artifacts flatly assert the opposite; (3) an unclassified claim riding alongside a proven one -- POLICY-EQUALITY-AND-COMPOSITION section 3 states the K join-semilattice claim as an aesthetic 'pleasing duality' aside, and its own formal classification table never lists the K claim at all (only the separately PROVEN, executed (Policy,meet) meet-semilattice claim), so an unclassified and unexecuted K-order claim was smuggled in beside a genuinely proven Policy-level one.

rows.anchor: *"Adding knowledge only grows the state"* requires monotone growth. The corpus has **withdrawal and retraction** ... and **EXECUTED** (`step-288/06 §H`) withdrawal **re-keys the assertion id and dangles every `ℛ`-edge**. $$\boxed{\text{Retraction shrinks. Monotone growth is REFUTED for } \mathbb K.}$$
rows.statement: Refutes the monotone-growth claim underlying the semilattice overclaim ('adding knowledge only grows the state') by execution: the corpus has withdrawal/retraction (Article 8, invariant I-12), and the previously executed test (step-288 06 section H) already showed withdrawal re-keys the assertion id and dangles every relational edge -- retraction shrinks the state rather than only ever growing it, so monotone growth for K is REFUTED, not merely unproven.

rows.anchor: | **extensional** | 🔴 no — and note it is **undecidable in general even for Policy** (`POLICY-EQUALITY` §2) | **semantic** | 🔴 no — *"NOT COMPUTABLE"* even for Policy ... $$\boxed{(Policy, \wedge) \text{ being a meet-semilattice establishes NOTHING about } \mathbb K.}$$
rows.statement: Tests whether any of four policy-level equality notions (identifier, structural, extensional, semantic) transfer to K, finding none do: K_t has no identity rule (identifier fails), K's canonicalization is unbound (structural fails), extensional policy equality is undecidable in general even for Policy itself, and semantic policy equality is explicitly 'NOT COMPUTABLE' even for Policy. Concludes (Policy, meet) being a meet-semilattice establishes nothing about K -- they are separate mathematical objects -- while noting two Policy findings DO generalize as methodology rather than algebra: 'policy equality != equal output' (agreement on a finite sample is not evidence, independently reproduced for equality generally) and 'version must be part of identity'.
invariants: (Policy, meet) being a meet-semilattice establishes nothing about K

experiment.hypothesis: Whether Steps 202-205 build on a single, well-formed Step 201.
experiment.setup: Full read of all files in the 158-205 range including byte-size and md5 comparison.
experiment.inputs: 78 files in scope, 56 fully read.
experiment.method: Direct comparison of two files both titled Step 201.
experiment.result: Two non-duplicate, mutually inconsistent Step-201 documents found; only one (201-A) is used downstream.
experiment.interpretation: The corpus's own downstream steps silently chose one of two competing self-declared 'Step 201' documents without acknowledging or resolving the fork.
experiment.limitations: Argument-level textual analysis, not automated verification.

sources.note: An implemented EKS runtime architecture (per the 2026-08-01 baseline) that decouples change-detection (ChangeSet, tool-agnostic) from observation execution (collectors such as LCOM4/test-presence) and recommendation generation/presentation; proposed as a strong KnowledgeOS-kernel integration candidate.

rows.anchor: ObservationTrigger → ChangeSet → ObservationRuntime → Collectors → Observations → Recommendation Engine → Presentation
rows.statement: Describes a demonstrated implemented runtime pipeline: a trigger (commit, file-save, Claude Code, VS Code) produces a ChangeSet that decouples event detection from observation execution; the runtime orchestrates collector execution and recommendation generation independent of trigger origin.
invariants: Capability and adapter are separate: a capability is not named after its current implementation technology.

rows.anchor: A current architectural decision is that events should carry references, not source code ... an observation event should conceptually contain commit_id, file reference, change metadata rather than embedding complete source code.
rows.statement: States the Event Payload Principle: events reference engineering artifacts rather than embedding source code, keeping the repository as the single source of truth and payloads small.
invariants: Repository remains source of truth: events reference engineering artifacts rather than embedding source code.

rows.statement: Elevates ChangeSet to a strong kernel-integration candidate because it already decouples change detection from observation execution regardless of tool origin (Git/VS Code/Claude Code/CI), proposing it sit below both EKS and PKS collectors.

rows.anchor: Measurement is not recommendation ... Kernel: Observation, Evidence, Rule evaluation protocol, Assessment, Result, Provenance / EKS: LCOM4 rule, Test-presence rule, Architecture rule, DDD rule, Engineering recommendation.

sources.note: Step 170's full end-to-end pipeline formalized as eight GATED (not automatic) transitions O-g1->E-g2->K-g3->D_t-g4->D_c-g5->A-g6->X-g7->R-g8->O', each S_i-G_i->S_{i+1} requiring a transition gate G_i, correcting any reading of the arrows as automatic causation (e.g. not every observation becomes evidence, not every piece of knowledge causes a decision). Splits the earlier undifferentiated 'Determination/Decision' pairing into explicit distinct symbols D_t (Determination) and D_c (Decision). Per-transition tuple definitions: O=<source,time,value,context>; E=<O,provenance,integrity,classification,scope> (E structurally contains O, 'the evidence layer enriches the observation'); K=<claim,basis,scope,validity,version>; a KnowledgeState(K) enumeration {Candidate,Supported,Established,Superseded,Contested,Invalidated}; D_t=f(K,Policy,Method,Context); Decision=f(Determination,GovernanceContext,Authority,Policy); Authorization as a relation Auth(actor,action,scope,time,policy), contextual not permanent, with the invariant Execute(a,x,t)=>Auth(a,x,s,t,p) and a temporal-ordering check AuthorizationGranted < ExecutionStarted unless retrospective authorization is explicitly domain-permitted; and a distinction Execution!=Outcome (ExecutionStatus vs OutcomeStatus kept separate, e.g. Execution=completed while BusinessOutcome=requirement-not-satisfied).

rows.anchor: S_i --G_i--> S_{i+1} where S_i = current state; G_i = transition gate; S_{i+1} = resulting state. ... O -g1-> E -g2-> K -g3-> D_t -g4-> D_c -g5-> A -g6-> X -g7-> R -g8-> O'. ... A Determination answers: Based on the available evidence and applicable reasoning, what do we conclude? A Decision answers: Given that determination and the relevant governance context, what shall we do? Thus: Determination ≠ Decision.
rows.statement: Reformalizes the full pipeline as eight explicitly gated transitions S_i --G_i--> S_{i+1} (O-g1->E-g2->K-g3->D_t-g4->D_c-g5->A-g6->X-g7->R-g8->O'), correcting any reading of the arrows as automatic causation; for the first time gives Determination (D_t) and Decision (D_c) fully distinct symbols throughout, with Determination answering 'what do we conclude' and Decision answering 'what shall we do' given that determination and governance context.

rows.statement: Gives explicit tuple definitions along the pipeline: O=<source,time,value,context>; E=<O,provenance,integrity,classification,scope> (E structurally contains O -- 'the evidence layer enriches the observation'), with a Reported!=Verified caution that not every observation should become evidence; K=<claim,basis,scope,validity,version> with a six-value KnowledgeState enumeration {Candidate,Supported,Established,Superseded,Contested,Invalidated} explicitly not final.

Authorized(a,x) is not a permanent property. It is contextual. ... Execute(a,x,t) ⇒ Auth(a,x,s,t,p). ... AuthorizationGranted < ExecutionStarted in temporal order. ... Execution ≠ Outcome. ... ExecutionStatus and OutcomeStatus ... should not be collapsed.
rows.statement: Continues the tuple formalization: D_t=f(K,Policy,Method,Context) (reproducible/inspectable); Decision=f(Determination,GovernanceContext,Authority,Policy), with AIRecommendation!=GovernanceDecision enforced at the transition gate; Authorization as the contextual relation Auth(actor,action,scope,time,policy), with Execute(a,x,t)=>Auth(a,x,s,t,p) and a temporal-ordering check AuthorizationGranted < ExecutionStarted (violated unless the domain explicitly permits retrospective authorization); and Execution!=Outcome, requiring separate ExecutionStatus and OutcomeStatus fields (e.g. Execution=completed while BusinessOutcome=requirement-not-satisfied is a legitimate joint state).

Who may initiate? Who may verify? Who may approve? Who may execute? Who is accountable? ... rows.statement: Step 170 verdict: the end-to-end chain is architecturally coherent, subject to domain-specific definitions and verification rules -- 'KnowledgeOS can be understood as a controlled transformation system between observation, evidence, knowledge, determination, decision, authority, action, and outcome', with the cycle closing Action->Outcome->Observation->Evidence->Knowledge'. Proposes Step 171 = Who Owns Each Transition?, constructing an Authority-Responsibility-Evidence matrix asking per transition who may initiate/verify/approve/execute and who is accountable, and flagging the anti-pattern 'one actor -> Generate -> Verify -> Approve -> Execute' as a single-point-of-trust problem.

sources.note: A reinterpretation of the proposal/challenge/reconciliation sexual metaphor treating 'orgasm' not as a state (rejecting Knowledge=orgasm=balance) but as a discrete ClosureEvent transition K_t -> K_{t+1}, with a worked Nexus-version example and a decisive negative test showing that numeric zero (+a plus -b = 0) is produced by at least six distinct and non-equivalent epistemic conditions (genuine balance, contradiction, insufficiency, incomparability, double-counted dependent evidence, temporally-distinct claims) -- concluding Numeric zero != Epistemic closure, and proposing a falsification-oriented KR-ORGASM research track to test whether Balanced/Reconciled/Determined/Known/Closed can be kept distinct while dynamically linked.

rows.anchor: Reconciliation != Knowledge and Orgasm = transition event and Knowledge = resulting epistemic state ... E_t --Reconciliation--> OrgasmEvent_t --Attribution--> K_{t+1}
rows.statement: Reframes 'orgasm' from a static balanced state to a discrete transition event (ClosureEvent) mapping an epistemic state to its successor via reconciliation and attribution, explicitly separating reconciliation from knowledge.

rows.anchor: +0.8 + (-0.8) = 0 ... A The evidence genuinely balances. B The evidence is contradictory. C The evidence is insufficient. D The evidence is incomparable. E ... double-counted. F ... concerns different times. All six produce something that looks like zero. ... Numeric zero != Epistemic closure.
rows.statement: Delivers the decisive negative test: at least six distinct and non-equivalent epistemic conditions (genuine balance, contradiction, insufficiency, incomparability, dependent double-counted evidence, temporally-distinct claims) all produce apparent numeric zero, so numeric zero cannot be identified with epistemic closure.

rows.anchor: Orgasm(Q,t) <=> Closure(Q,t) and Reconciled(Q,t) and Adequate(Q,t) and Stable(Q,t) but Closure, Reconciled, and Stable are themselves currently open concepts. So we should not pretend we have solved them.
rows.statement: Proposes a research-hypothesis (not definition) formal criterion for an 'epistemic orgasm'/closure event conjoining four currently-open sub-concepts, explicitly flagging that none of the four is yet solved.

rows.anchor: KR-ORGASM-2026-09-02 ... Can epistemic orgasm be operationalized as a closure event generated by proposal-challenge-reconciliation dynamics without collapsing Zero, determination, truth, or knowledge into one state? ... 15 test cases ... If they collapse into one state, the metaphor is too crude.
rows.statement: Proposes a falsification-oriented KR-ORGASM research track with 15 named adversarial test cases, whose success criterion is whether Balanced/Reconciled/Determined/Known/Closed remain distinguishable while dynamically linked by the closure event.

experiment.hypothesis: an inquiry may be modelled as a generative proposal/challenge interaction producing a discrete closure event that yields a revised epistemic state, without collapsing Zero/determination/truth/knowledge into one state
experiment.setup: proposal-challenge-evidence-assessment-reconciliation pipeline over a synthetic inquiry (e.g. software version determination)
experiment.assumptions: the sexual metaphor's proposal/challenge/reconciliation/climax stages can be mapped onto epistemic transitions without literal reproduction being implied
experiment.inputs: 15 named test cases: no proposal, proposal without challenge, weak/strong challenge, balanced/contradictory/dependent evidence, underdetermined hypotheses, unobservable target, model misspecification, multiple hypotheses, successful determination, successful attribution, new evidence after closure, retrospective revision
experiment.method: not yet run -- proposed as a research track, KR-ORGASM-2026-09-02
experiment.interpretation: if Balanced/Reconciled/Determined/Known/Closed collapse into one state under testing, the metaphor is too crude; if they remain distinguishable while dynamically linked, something useful has been discovered
experiment.limitations: entirely a proposed, not-yet-executed research design
experiment.conclusion: the KR-ORGASM track is recommended but not run in this document

sources.note: Yin-Yang-lens reframing of evidence collection as inherently two-sided: SupportingObservations, ContradictingObservations, MissingObservations, AlternativeExplanations, ContextualConditions must all be actively sought, not only observations that support a hypothesis; expanded later in the file into a fuller EvidenceInquiry object with Question/Claim/Decision Context/Target Phenomenon/Acquisition Intent/Selection Procedure/Observation Procedure/Measurement Context/Observer{identity,role,authority}/Situation{time,environment,actors,constraints}/Expected/Contradicting/Alternative/Deviations/Resulting Observations.

rows.anchor: There is always a complementary side: supporting observation vs contradicting observation ... a serious Evidence Acquisition process should actively collect both sides. ... EvidenceInquiry: SupportingObservations, ContradictingObservations, MissingObservations, AlternativeExplanations, ContextualConditions.
rows.statement: Yin-Yang lens: evidence acquisition should have a built-in polarity, actively seeking both observations that illuminate a hypothesis and observations that could undermine it, rather than only 'find evidence for H'; formalized as an EvidenceInquiry object; noted as compatible with Achinstein's competing-explanations requirement and with causal inference.

rows.anchor: Someone asks the question, chooses the measurement, selects the sample, interprets the result, decides whether the result is sufficient, acts upon it. ... WHO ... not simply as an identity field, but as: ROLE, AUTHORITY, RESPONSIBILITY, PURPOSE.
rows.statement: Confucian lens: the observer's role/authority/responsibility/purpose (not merely identity) must be preserved, illustrated by contrasting a security-engineer/independent-auditor compliance observation with the same observation made by a marketing team for marketing material, which carries a different epistemic context.

rows.anchor: This does NOT mean 'trust the person'. ... The role and relationship of the observer are themselves part of the situation that must be known.
rows.statement: Explicit correction guarding against misreading the Confucian observer-role lens as 'trust the person': the observer's role/relationship is itself part of the knowable situation, not a substitute for evidence, and this is stated to be compatible with Achinstein's claim that evidence statements can depend on empirical facts about the epistemic situation.

rows.anchor: The AI should not primarily be an evidence collector. It should be an Epistemic Inquiry Assistant. ... Only then: collect / search / measure.
rows.statement: Reframes AI's role from evidence collector to 'Epistemic Inquiry Assistant' whose job is to ask what we're trying to know, how something was observed, what was selected/excluded, what the situation was, what changed, what would contradict the claim, what alternatives exist, what remains unknown, and what evidence would reduce uncertainty -- only afterward collecting/searching/measuring; extended into an agent workflow (Question->Inquiry Formulation->Evidence Need->Acquisition Design->Collection->Provenance Capture->Selection Audit->Contradiction Search->Alternative Explanation->Evidence Assessment->Knowledge Update) that a Verification Engine should confirm was not bypassed.

sources.note: Step 182's central proposition: 'authority is bounded' by Domain, Proposition/DecisionType, Scope, Time, Context -- no actor or system possesses universal organizational authority, and no single AuthorityLevel number is meaningful (Authority=10 is meaningless without 'authority for what'; must be Authority(a,Action,Scope,Time)). Applies this reflexively to KnowledgeOS itself: it may be authoritative as RecordOfDecision but not as CurrentOperationalReality, and may store an ArchitectureDecision without possessing AuthorityToChangeProduction -- 'the knowledge repository records authority; it does not automatically possess authority', preventing the system from becoming a hidden governance mechanism. Applies this to AI specifically: retrieving Decision=Approved does not let an AI infer 'I am authorized to execute' -- AuthorizationValid must be separately established, an agent-operating-contract requirement. States the platform's proper structural-enforcement role via a type-system analogy: 'KnowledgeOS enforces the integrity of governance artifacts; domain governance defines what those artifacts mean' -- the platform can enforce 'this object must have valid structure' (e.g. EveryDecisionHasAuthorityBasis, EveryDeterminationHasEvidenceBasis, EveryAuthorizationHasScope, EveryHistoricalArtifactHasTemporalContext) without inventing the domain rules themselves.

sources.note: Step 187 formalizes the four Step-186-proposed concepts as distinct parameterized relations: Cap(a,x) (technical capability, e.g. Cap(AI,WriteKnowledgeRecord)=1), Perm(a,x,c,t) (access-control permission, e.g. an AI permitted to CreateCandidate but not ApproveDecision), Auth(a,d,c,t) (legitimate domain/governance authority over a determination d, with Perm(a,x) not implying Auth(a,d) -- worked DBA example: write permission without architecture-approval authority), Resp(a,d,c,t) (accountability, with Auth(a,d) not implying Resp(a,d) -- a board may hold authority while a named role holds operational responsibility). Explicitly rejects the common architectural mistake of assuming a linear implication chain Cap=>Perm=>Auth=>Resp as FALSE -- these may correlate but must never be inferred from one another. Formalizes Auth(a,r,c,t)=f(Role,Scope,Delegation,Rule,t,c), stating the function f belongs to the governance model, not the mathematical kernel itself, and that a Role alone (e.g. Role(A)=Architect) does not imply blanket authority.

rows.statement: 19.77-19.80: Theorem 19.1 (Contractual Reconstruction) -- if persistence preserves all EC-required distinctions/provenance/temporal/version/history information, a reconstruction function Rec_EC exists with Rec_EC(P(K_t))≡_EC K_t (semantic equivalence, not structural identity -- Rec(P(K))=K is 'unnecessarily strong'); Theorem 19.2 (Projection Adequacy) -- a query-Q projection R_Q(K) is contractually adequate for Q iff Loss_Q∩Dist_EC(Q)=∅, i.e. a projection need only preserve what its query contract requires; Theorem 19.3 (History Preservation) -- if persistence stores a transition o with all semantic replay dependencies, Replay(H_t,V_t)≡_Gamma K_t under the applicable replay contract; Theorem 19.4 (Semantic Migration) -- a migration M:R1->R2 is semantically preserving iff Sem(R1)≡_Gamma Sem(R2) for all required contracts, otherwise it represents semantic change or loss, so SchemaMigration must be evaluated separately from SemanticMigration.
